145	def _is_glob(path):
146	    return get_first_pos_of_char('*', path) > -1 or get_first_pos_of_char('?', path) > -1
147	
148	
149	def _rel2abs(path, project):
150	    if path.startswith('/') or dxpy.WORKSPACE_ID != project:
151	        abs_path, strip_prefix = path, os.path.dirname(path.rstrip('/'))
152	    else:
153	        wd = dxpy.config.get('DX_CLI_WD', u'/')
154	        abs_path, strip_prefix = os.path.join(wd, path), os.path.dirname(os.path.join(wd, path).rstrip('/'))
155	    if len(abs_path) > 1:
156	        abs_path = abs_path.rstrip('/')
157	    return abs_path, strip_prefix
158	
159	
160	def _download_files(files, destdir, args, dest_filename=None):
161	    for project in files:
162	        for f in files[project]:
163	            file_desc = f['describe']
164	            dest = dest_filename or os.path.join(destdir, file_desc['name'].replace('/', '%2F'))
165	            download_one_file(project, file_desc, dest, args)
166	
167	
168	def _download_folders(folders, destdir, args):
169	    try:
170	        show_progress = args.show_progress
171	    except AttributeError:
172	        show_progress = False
173	    for project in folders:
174	        for folder, strip_prefix in folders[project]:
175	            if not args.recursive:
176	                err_exit('Error: "' + folder + '" is a folder but the -r/--recursive option was not given')
177	            assert(folder.startswith(strip_prefix))
178	            folder_destdir = os.path.join(destdir, folder[len(strip_prefix):].lstrip('/'))
179	            try:
180	                dxpy.download_folder(project, folder_destdir, folder=folder, overwrite=args.overwrite,
181	                                     show_progress=show_progress)
182	            except:
183	                err_exit()
184	
185	
186	# Main entry point.
187	def download(args):
188	    folders_to_get, files_to_get, count = collections.defaultdict(list), collections.defaultdict(list), 0
189	    foldernames, filenames = [], []
190	    for path in args.paths:
191	        # Attempt to resolve name. If --all is given or the path looks like a glob, download all matches.
192	        # Otherwise, the resolver will display a picker (or error out if there is no tty to display to).
193	        resolver_kwargs = {'allow_empty_string': False}
194	        if args.all or _is_glob(path):
195	            resolver_kwargs.update({'allow_mult': True, 'all_mult': True})
196	
197	        # include "parts" and a few additional fields in the description so that
198	        # we don't have to call a separate describe method downstream
199	        resolver_kwargs.update({"describe": {"parts": True,
200	                                             "size": True,
201	                                             "drive": True,
202	                                             "md5": True,
203	                                             "checksumType": True
204	                                             }})
205	
206	        project, folderpath, matching_files = try_call(resolve_existing_path, path, **resolver_kwargs)
207	
208	        if matching_files is None:
209	            matching_files = []
210	        elif not isinstance(matching_files, list):
211	            matching_files = [matching_files]
212	
213	        # TODO: this could also be returned as metadata by resolve_path since
214	        # resolve_path knows these things in some circumstances
215	        path_has_explicit_proj = is_project_explicit(path) or is_jbor_str(path)
216	
217	        if is_jbor_str(path):
218	            assert len(matching_files) == 1
219	            project = matching_files[0]["describe"]["project"]
220	        matching_folders = []
221	        # project may be none if path is an ID and there is no project context
222	        if project is not None:
223	            colon_pos = get_first_pos_of_char(":", path)
224	            if colon_pos >= 0:
225	                path = path[colon_pos + 1:]
226	            abs_path, strip_prefix = _rel2abs(path, project)
227	            parent_folder = os.path.dirname(abs_path)
228	            folder_listing = dxpy.list_subfolders(project, parent_folder, recurse=False)
229	            matching_folders = pathmatch.filter(folder_listing, abs_path)
230	            if '/' in matching_folders and len(matching_folders) > 1:
231	                # The list of subfolders is {'/', '/A', '/B'}.
232	                # Remove '/', otherwise we will download everything twice.
233	                matching_folders.remove('/')
234	
235	        if len(matching_files) == 0 and len(matching_folders) == 0:
236	            err_exit(fill('Error: {path} is neither a file nor a folder name'.format(path=path)))
237	
238	        # If the user did not explicitly provide the project, don't pass any
239	        # project parameter to the API call but continue with the download.
240	        if not path_has_explicit_proj:
241	            project = dxpy.DXFile.NO_PROJECT_HINT
242	
243	        # If the user explicitly provided the project and it doesn't contain
244	        # the files, don't allow the download.
245	
246	        # For speed's sake, skip this check (i.e. one API call) if the user
247	        # passed the lightweight argument
248	        #
249	        # If length of matching_files is 0 then we're only downloading folders
250	        # so skip this logic since the files will be verified in the API call.
251	        if not args.lightweight \
252	            and len(matching_files) > 0 \
253	            and path_has_explicit_proj \
254	            and not any(object_exists_in_project(f['describe']['id'], project) for f in matching_files):
255	                err_exit(fill('Error: specified project does not contain specified file object'))
256	
257	        files_to_get[project].extend(matching_files)
258	        folders_to_get[project].extend(((f, strip_prefix) for f in matching_folders))
259	        count += len(matching_files) + len(matching_folders)
260	        filenames.extend(f["describe"]["name"] for f in matching_files)
261	        foldernames.extend(f[len(strip_prefix):].lstrip('/') for f in matching_folders)
262	
263	    if len(filenames) > 0 and len(foldernames) > 0:
264	        name_conflicts = set(filenames) & set(foldernames)
265	        if len(name_conflicts) > 0:
266	            msg = "Error: The following paths are both file and folder names, and " \
267	                  "cannot be downloaded to the same destination: "
268	            msg += ", ".join(sorted(name_conflicts))
269	            err_exit(fill(msg))
270	
271	    if args.output is None:
272	        destdir, dest_filename = os.getcwd(), None
273	    elif count > 1:
274	        if not os.path.exists(args.output):
275	            err_exit(fill("Error: When downloading multiple objects, --output must be an existing directory"))
276	        destdir, dest_filename = args.output, None
277	    elif os.path.isdir(args.output):
278	        destdir, dest_filename = args.output, None
279	    elif args.output.endswith('/'):
280	        err_exit(fill("Error: {path} could not be found".format(path=args.output)))
281	    else:
282	        destdir, dest_filename = os.getcwd(), args.output
283	
284	    _download_folders(folders_to_get, destdir, args)
285	    _download_files(files_to_get, destdir, args, dest_filename=dest_filename)

86	def get_folder_matches(text, delim_pos, dxproj, folderpath):
87	    '''
88	    :param text: String to be tab-completed; still in escaped form
89	    :type text: string

91	    :type delim_pos: int

95	    :type folderpath: string

98	
99	    Members of the returned list are guaranteed to start with *text*
100	    and be in escaped form for consumption by the command-line.
101	    '''
102	    try:
103	        folders = dxproj.list_folder(folder=folderpath, only='folders')['folders']
104	        folder_names = [name[name.rfind('/') + 1:] for name in folders]
105	        if text != '' and delim_pos != len(text) - 1:
106	            folder_names += ['.', '..']

108	        return [prefix + f + '/' for f in folder_names if (prefix + f + '/').startswith(text)]

158	def path_completer(text, expected=None, classes=None, perm_level=None,
159	                   include_current_proj=False, typespec=None, visibility=None):
160	    '''
161	    :param text: String to tab-complete to a path matching the syntax project-name:folder/entity_or_folder_name
162	    :type text: string
163	    :param expected: "folder", "entity", "project", or None (no restriction) as to the types of answers to look for
164	    :type expected: string
165	    :param classes: if expected="entity", the possible data object classes that are acceptable
166	    :type classes: list of strings
167	    :param perm_level: the minimum permissions level required, e.g. "VIEW" or "CONTRIBUTE"
168	    :type perm_level: string
169	    :param include_current_proj: Indicate whether the current project's name should be a potential result
170	    :type include_current_proj: boolean
171	    :param visibility: Visibility with which to restrict the completion (one of "either", "visible", or "hidden") (default behavior is dependent on *text*)
172	
173	    Returns a list of matches to the text and restricted by the
174	    requested parameters.
175	    '''
176	    colon_pos = get_last_pos_of_char(':', text)
177	    slash_pos = get_last_pos_of_char('/', text)
178	    delim_pos = max(colon_pos, slash_pos)
179	
180	    # First get projects if necessary
181	    matches = []
182	    if expected == 'project' and colon_pos > 0 and colon_pos == len(text) - 1:
183	        if dxpy.find_one_project(zero_ok=True, name=text[:colon_pos]) is not None:
184	            return [text + " "]
185	
186	    if colon_pos < 0 and slash_pos < 0:
187	        # Might be tab-completing a project, but don't ever include
188	        # whatever's set as dxpy.WORKSPACE_ID unless expected == "project"
189	        # Also, don't bother if text=="" and expected is NOT "project"
190	        # Also, add space if expected == "project"
191	        if text != "" or expected == 'project':
192	            results = dxpy.find_projects(describe=True, level=perm_level)
193	            if not include_current_proj:
194	                results = [r for r in results if r['id'] != dxpy.WORKSPACE_ID]
195	            matches += [escape_colon(r['describe']['name'])+':' for r in results if r['describe']['name'].startswith(text)]
196	
197	    if expected == 'project':
198	        return matches
199	
200	    # Attempt to tab-complete to a folder or data object name
201	    if colon_pos < 0 and slash_pos >= 0:
202	        # Not tab-completing a project, and the project is unambiguous
203	        # (use dxpy.WORKSPACE_ID)
204	        if dxpy.WORKSPACE_ID is not None:
205	            # try-catch block in case dxpy.WORKSPACE_ID is garbage
206	            try:
207	                dxproj = dxpy.get_handler(dxpy.WORKSPACE_ID)
208	                folderpath, entity_name = clean_folder_path(text)
209	                matches += get_folder_matches(text, slash_pos, dxproj, folderpath)

211	                    if classes is not None:

214	                                                        folderpath, classname=classname,

217	                    else:

219	                                                    folderpath, typespec=typespec,
220	                                                    visibility=visibility)
221	            except:
222	                pass
223	    else:
224	        # project is given by a path, but attempt to resolve to an

47	class DXConfig(MutableMapping):
48	    """This class provides the dxpy configuration manager, available as
49	    ``dxpy.config``. When first accessed, the config manager looks up
50	    environment variables used to configure dxpy, and if they are not
51	    found, then attempts to resolve them by looking in the file
52	    ~/.dnanexus_config/environment, followed by the installed defaults
53	    in /etc/dnanexus.
54	
55	    To assign to and access variables managed by the configuration
56	    manager, use ``dxpy.config["VAR_NAME"]``. When assigning a
57	    variable, the manager sets it as a process environment variable
58	    and updates any dxpy variable bound to it
59	    (e.g. dxpy.SECURITY_CONTEXT when setting
60	    DX_SECURITY_CONTEXT). When accessing a variable, it is looked up
61	    from the process environment.
62	
63	    To save (serialize) the value of a variable to a persistent dxpy
64	    configuration file, use ``dxpy.config.write(key, value)`` or
65	    ``dxpy.config.save()`` after assigning variable values. To clear
66	    the values in persistent dxpy configuration, use
67	    ``dxpy.config.clear()``.
68	    """
69	    CORE_VAR_NAMES = {"DX_APISERVER_HOST", "DX_APISERVER_PORT",
70	                      "DX_APISERVER_PROTOCOL", "DX_PROJECT_CONTEXT_ID",
71	                      "DX_WORKSPACE_ID", "DX_SECURITY_CONTEXT", "DX_JOB_ID"}
72	    STANDALONE_VAR_NAMES = {"DX_CLI_WD", "DX_USERNAME",
73	                            "DX_PROJECT_CONTEXT_NAME"}
74	    """
75	    List of variable names supported by the configuration manager.
76	    """
77	    VAR_NAMES = set.union(CORE_VAR_NAMES, STANDALONE_VAR_NAMES)
78	    defaults = {
79	        "DX_SECURITY_CONTEXT": json.dumps({"auth_token": "PUBLIC", "auth_token_type": "Bearer"}),
80	        "DX_APISERVER_PROTOCOL": DEFAULT_APISERVER_PROTOCOL,
81	        "DX_APISERVER_HOST": DEFAULT_APISERVER_HOST,
82	        "DX_APISERVER_PORT": DEFAULT_APISERVER_PORT,
83	        "DX_CLI_WD": "/"
84	    }
85	    _global_conf_dir = "/etc/dnanexus"
86	
87	    def __init__(self, suppress_warning=False):
88	        """
89	        :param suppress_warning:
90	            Whether to suppress the warning message for any mismatch found in the environment variables and the dx
91	            configuration file
92	        :type suppress_warning: boolean
93	        """
94	        try:
95	            dxpy._DEBUG = int(os.environ.get("_DX_DEBUG", 0))
96	        except ValueError as e:
97	            warn("WARNING: Expected _DX_DEBUG to be an integer, but got", os.environ["_DX_DEBUG"])
98	            dxpy._DEBUG = 0
99	
100	        try:
101	            dxpy._INJECT_ERROR = bool(os.environ.get("_DX_INJECT_ERROR", 0))
102	        except:
103	            dxpy._INJECT_ERROR = False
104	
105	        self._user_conf_dir = os.path.expanduser(os.environ.get("DX_USER_CONF_DIR", "~/.dnanexus_config"))
106	
107	        dxpy._UPGRADE_NOTIFY = os.path.join(self._user_conf_dir, ".upgrade_notify")
108	        # If last upgrade notification was less than 24 hours ago, disable it
109	        if os.path.exists(dxpy._UPGRADE_NOTIFY) and os.path.getmtime(dxpy._UPGRADE_NOTIFY) > time.time() - 86400:
110	            dxpy._UPGRADE_NOTIFY = False
111	
112	        env_vars = self._read_conf_dir(self.get_global_conf_dir())
113	        env_vars.update(self._read_conf_dir(self.get_user_conf_dir()))
114	        env_vars.update(self._read_conf_dir(self.get_session_conf_dir(cleanup=True)))
115	        env_overrides = []
116	        for var in self.VAR_NAMES:
117	            if var in os.environ:
118	                if var in env_vars and env_vars.get(var) != os.environ[var]:
119	                    env_overrides.append(var)
120	                env_vars[var] = os.environ[var]
121	
122	        for var in env_vars:
123	            if env_vars[var] is not None:
124	                os.environ[var] = env_vars[var]
125	
126	        if sys.stdout.isatty():
127	            if not suppress_warning and len(env_overrides) > 0:
128	                msg = "WARNING: The following environment variables were found to be different than the values " + \
129	                      "last stored by dx: "
130	                warn(fill(msg + ", ".join(env_overrides), width=80))
131	                msg = "To use the values stored by dx, unset the environment variables in your shell by running " + \
132	                      '"source ~/.dnanexus_config/unsetenv".  To clear the dx-stored values, run "dx clearenv".'
133	                warn(fill(msg, width=80))

137	    def _sync_dxpy_state(self):

139	                                 port=os.environ.get("DX_APISERVER_PORT", None),

141	
142	        if "DX_SECURITY_CONTEXT" in os.environ:
143	            dxpy.set_security_context(json.loads(os.environ["DX_SECURITY_CONTEXT"]))
144	
145	        if "DX_JOB_ID" in os.environ:
146	            dxpy.set_job_id(os.environ["DX_JOB_ID"])
147	            dxpy.set_workspace_id(os.environ.get("DX_WORKSPACE_ID"))
148	        else:
149	            dxpy.set_job_id(None)
150	            dxpy.set_workspace_id(os.environ.get("DX_PROJECT_CONTEXT_ID"))
151	        
152	        if "DX_WATCH_PORT" in os.environ:
153	            dxpy.set_watch_port(os.environ.get("DX_WATCH_PORT"))
154	        else:
155	            dxpy.set_watch_port(None)
156	
157	        dxpy.set_project_context(os.environ.get("DX_PROJECT_CONTEXT_ID"))

159	    def get_global_conf_dir(self):
160	        return self._global_conf_dir
161	
162	    def get_user_conf_dir(self):
163	        return self._user_conf_dir
164	
165	    def get_session_conf_dir(self, cleanup=False):
166	        """
167	        Tries to find the session configuration directory by looking in ~/.dnanexus_config/sessions/<PID>,
168	        where <PID> is pid of the parent of this process, then its parent, and so on.
169	        If none of those exist, the path for the immediate parent is given, even if it doesn't exist.
170	
171	        If *cleanup* is True, looks up and deletes all session configuration directories that belong to nonexistent
172	        processes.
173	        """
174	        sessions_dir = os.path.join(self._user_conf_dir, "sessions")
175	        try:
176	            from psutil import Process, pid_exists
177	
178	            if cleanup:
179	                try:
180	                    session_dirs = os.listdir(sessions_dir)
181	                except OSError as e:
182	                    # Silently skip cleanup and continue if we are unable to
183	                    # enumerate the session directories for any reason
184	                    # (including, most commonly, because the sessions dir
185	                    # doesn't exist)
186	                    session_dirs = []
187	                for session_dir in session_dirs:
188	                    try:
189	                        session_pid = int(session_dir)
190	                    except ValueError:
191	                        # If dir name doesn't look like an int, leave it
192	                        # alone
193	                        continue
194	                    if not pid_exists(session_pid):
195	                        rmtree(os.path.join(sessions_dir, session_dir), ignore_errors=True)
196	
197	            parent_process = Process(os.getpid()).parent()
198	            if parent_process is None:
199	                parent_process = Process(os.getpid())
200	            default_session_dir = os.path.join(sessions_dir, str(parent_process.pid))
201	            while parent_process is not None and parent_process.pid != 0:
202	                session_dir = os.path.join(sessions_dir, str(parent_process.pid))
203	                if os.path.exists(session_dir):
204	                    return session_dir
205	                parent_process = parent_process.parent()
206	            return default_session_dir
207	        except (ImportError, IOError, AttributeError) as e:
208	            # We don't bundle psutil with Windows, so failure to import
209	            # psutil would be expected.
210	            if platform.system() != 'Windows':
211	                warn(fill("Error while retrieving session configuration: " + format_exception(e)))
212	        except Exception as e:
213	            warn(fill("Unexpected error while retrieving session configuration: " + format_exception(e)))
214	        return self._get_ppid_session_conf_dir(sessions_dir)
215	
216	    def _get_ppid_session_conf_dir(self, sessions_dir):
217	        try:
218	            return os.path.join(sessions_dir, str(os.getppid()))
219	        except AttributeError:
220	            pass # os.getppid is not available on Windows
221	        except Exception as e:
222	            warn(fill("Unexpected error while retrieving session configuration: " + format_exception(e)))
223	        return os.path.join(sessions_dir, str(os.getpid()))

225	    def _read_conf_dir(self, dirname):
226	        try:
227	            with open(os.path.join(dirname, "environment.json")) as fd:
228	                env_vars = json.load(fd)
229	        except Exception:
230	            env_vars = {}
231	
232	        for standalone_var in self.STANDALONE_VAR_NAMES:
233	            try:
234	                with open(os.path.join(dirname, standalone_var)) as fd:
235	                    env_vars[standalone_var] = fd.read()
236	            except Exception:
237	                pass
238	        return env_vars

240	    def __getitem__(self, item):
241	        if item not in self.VAR_NAMES:
242	            raise KeyError(item)
243	        return os.environ[item]
244	
245	    def __setitem__(self, key, value):
246	        if key not in self.VAR_NAMES:
247	            raise KeyError(key)
248	        if value is None:
249	            value = self.defaults.get(key, "")
250	        os.environ[key] = value
251	        if key in self.CORE_VAR_NAMES:
252	            self._sync_dxpy_state()
253	
254	    def __delitem__(self, key):
255	        if key not in self.VAR_NAMES:
256	            raise KeyError(key)
257	        del os.environ[key]
258	        if key in self.CORE_VAR_NAMES:
259	            self._sync_dxpy_state()
260	
261	    def __iter__(self):
262	        for item in self.VAR_NAMES:
263	            if item in os.environ:
264	                yield item
265	
266	    def __len__(self):
267	        return len([var for var in self.VAR_NAMES if var in os.environ])
268	
269	    def __repr__(self):
270	        desc = "<{module}.{classname} object at 0x{mem_loc:x}: {data}>"
271	        return desc.format(module=self.__module__,
272	                           classname=self.__class__.__name__,
273	                           mem_loc=id(self),
274	                           data=dict(self))
275	
276	    def write(self, item, value):
277	        self[item] = value
278	        self.save()

283	        self._write_unsetenv(self._user_conf_dir)

285	    def _write_unsetenv(self, conf_dir):
286	        if not os.path.exists(os.path.join(conf_dir, "unsetenv")):
287	            with open(os.path.join(conf_dir, "unsetenv"), "w") as fd:
288	                fd.writelines("unset {}\n".format(var) for var in self.CORE_VAR_NAMES)

290	    def _write_conf_dir(self, conf_dir):
291	        try:
292	            os.makedirs(conf_dir, 0o700)
293	        except OSError:
294	            try:
295	                os.chmod(conf_dir, 0o700)
296	            except OSError as e:
297	                warn(fill("Error while writing configuration data: " + format_exception(e)))

301	        # Make sure the file has 600 permissions
302	        with _open_for_writing_with_permissions(env_jsonfile_path, 0o600) as fd:
303	            json.dump({k: self.get(k, self.defaults.get(k)) for k in self}, fd, indent=4)

307	            # Make sure the file has 600 permissions

309	                value = self.get(var, self.defaults.get(var, ""))
310	                fd.write(value)

50	    None values are written as empty strings by default (csv.DictWriter behavior)
51	
52	    """
53	
54	    IS_OS_WINDOWS = os.name == "nt"
55	    OS_SPECIFIC_LINE_SEPARATOR = os.linesep
56	    IS_PYTHON_2 = sys.version_info.major == 2
57	    IS_PYTHON_3 = sys.version_info.major == 3
58	
59	    if arg_sql:
60	        SUFFIX = ".sql"
61	        if not isinstance(output_listdict_or_string, str):
62	            error_handler("Expected SQL query to be a string")
63	    elif arg_delim:
64	        if arg_delim == ",":
65	            SUFFIX = ".csv"
66	        elif arg_delim == "\t":
67	            SUFFIX = ".tsv"
68	        else:
69	            if save_uncommon_delim_to_txt:
70	                SUFFIX = ".txt"
71	            else:
72	                error_handler("Unsupported delimiter: {}".format(arg_delim))
73	    else:
74	        SUFFIX = ".csv"
75	
76	    if arg_output:
77	        if arg_output == "-":
78	            WRITE_METHOD = "STDOUT"
79	        else:
80	            WRITE_METHOD = "FILE"
81	            output_file_name = arg_output
82	
83	    else:
84	        OUTPUT_DIR = os.getcwd()
85	
86	        if output_file_name is None:
87	            error_handler(
88	                "No output filename specified"
89	            )  # Developer expected to provide record_name upstream when calling this function
90	
91	        else:
92	            WRITE_METHOD = "FILE"
93	            output_file_name = os.path.join(OUTPUT_DIR, output_file_name + SUFFIX)
94	
95	    if WRITE_METHOD == "FILE":
96	        # error out if file already exists or output_file_name is a directory
97	        if os.path.exists(output_file_name):
98	            if os.path.isfile(output_file_name):
99	                error_handler(
100	                    "{} already exists. Please specify a new file path".format(
101	                        output_file_name
102	                    )
103	                )
104	            if os.path.isdir(output_file_name):
105	                error_handler(
106	                    "{} is a directory. Please specify a new file path".format(
107	                        output_file_name
108	                    )
109	                )
110	
111	    if arg_sql:
112	        if WRITE_METHOD == "STDOUT":
113	            print(output_listdict_or_string)
114	        elif WRITE_METHOD == "FILE":
115	            with open(output_file_name, "w") as f:
116	                f.write(output_listdict_or_string)
117	        else:
118	            error_handler("Unexpected error occurred while writing SQL query output")
119	
120	    else:
121	        if colnames:
122	            COLUMN_NAMES = colnames
123	        else:
124	            COLUMN_NAMES = output_listdict_or_string[0].keys()
125	
126	        if not all(
127	            set(i.keys()) == set(COLUMN_NAMES) for i in output_listdict_or_string
128	        ):
129	            error_handler("All rows must have the same column names")
130	
131	        WRITE_MODE = "wb" if IS_PYTHON_2 or IS_OS_WINDOWS else "w"
132	        NEWLINE = "" if IS_PYTHON_3 else None
133	        DELIMITER = str(arg_delim) if arg_delim else ","
134	        QUOTING = csv.QUOTE_MINIMAL
135	        QUOTE_CHAR = '"'
136	
137	        write_args = {
138	            "mode": WRITE_MODE,
139	        }
140	
141	        if IS_PYTHON_3:
142	            write_args["newline"] = NEWLINE
143	
144	        dictwriter_params = {
145	            "fieldnames": COLUMN_NAMES,
146	            "delimiter": DELIMITER,
147	            "lineterminator": OS_SPECIFIC_LINE_SEPARATOR,
148	            "quoting": QUOTING,
149	            "quotechar": QUOTE_CHAR,
150	        }
151	
152	        if WRITE_METHOD == "FILE":
153	            with open(output_file_name, **write_args) as f:
154	                w = csv.DictWriter(f, **dictwriter_params)
155	                w.writeheader()
156	                w.writerows(output_listdict_or_string)
157	
158	        elif WRITE_METHOD == "STDOUT":
159	            w = csv.DictWriter(sys.stdout, **dictwriter_params)
160	            w.writeheader()
161	            w.writerows(output_listdict_or_string)
162	
163	        else:
164	            error_handler("Unexpected error occurred while writing output")

23	from __future__ import print_function, unicode_literals, division, absolute_import
24	
25	import dxpy
26	from . import DXObject, DXAnalysis, DXExecutable, verify_string_dxid

34	
35	class DXGlobalWorkflow(DXObject, DXExecutable):
36	    '''
37	    Remote global workflow object handler.
38	    '''
39	
40	    _class = "globalworkflow"
41	
42	    def __init__(self, dxid=None, name=None, alias=None):
43	        DXObject.__init__(self)
44	        if dxid is not None or name is not None:
45	            self.set_id(dxid=dxid, name=name, alias=alias)
46	
47	        # caches for underlying workflow instances and descriptions per region
48	        # (they are immutable for a given global workflow)
49	        self._workflows_by_region = {}
50	        self._workflow_desc_by_region = {}
51	
52	    def set_id(self, dxid=None, name=None, alias=None):
53	        '''
54	        :param dxid: Global workflow ID
55	        :type dxid: string
56	        :param name: Global workflow name
57	        :type name: string
58	        :param alias: Global workflow version or tag
59	        :type alias: string
60	        :raises: :exc:`~dxpy.exceptions.DXError` if *dxid* and some other input are both given or if neither *dxid* nor *name* are given
61	
62	        Discards the currently stored ID and associates the handler
63	        with the requested parameters.  Note that if *dxid* is given,
64	        the other fields should not be given, and if *name* is given,
65	        *alias* has default value "default".
66	
67	        '''
68	        self._dxid = None
69	        self._name = None
70	        self._alias = None
71	        if dxid is not None:
72	            if name is not None or alias is not None:
73	                raise DXError("Did not expect name or alias to be given if dxid is given")
74	            verify_string_dxid(dxid, self._class)
75	            self._dxid = dxid
76	        elif name is not None:
77	            self._name = name
78	            if not isinstance(name, basestring):
79	                raise DXError("Global workflow name needs to be a string: %r" % (name,))
80	            if alias is not None:
81	                if not isinstance(alias, basestring):
82	                    raise DXError("Global workflow alias needs to be a string: %r" % (alias,))
83	                self._alias = alias
84	            else:
85	                self._alias = 'default'
86	
87	    def get_id(self):
88	        '''
89	        :returns: Object ID of associated global workflow
90	        :rtype: string
91	
92	        Returns the object ID of the global workflow that the handler is currently
93	        associated with.
94	        '''
95	        if self._dxid is not None:
96	            return self._dxid
97	        else:
98	            return 'globalworkflow-' + self._name + '/' + self._alias
99	
100	    def new(self, **kwargs):
101	        '''
102	
103	        .. note:: It is highly recommended that `dx build --create-global-workflow
104	           <https://documentation.dnanexus.com/user/helpstrings-of-sdk-command-line-utilities#build>`_
105	           be used instead for global workflow creation.
106	
107	        Creates a workflow in the global space with the given parameters by using
108	        the specified workflow(s) in regionalOptions as a base.
109	
110	        The workflow is available only to its developers until
111	        :meth:`publish()` is called, and is not run until :meth:`run()`
112	        is called.
113	
114	        '''
115	        dx_hash = {}
116	
117	        for field in ['version', 'name', 'regionalOptions']:
118	            if field not in kwargs:
119	                raise DXError("%s: Keyword argument %s is required" % (self.__class__.__name__, field))
120	            dx_hash[field] = kwargs[field]
121	            del kwargs[field]
122	
123	        if "bill_to" in kwargs:
124	            dx_hash['billTo'] = kwargs['bill_to']
125	            del kwargs["bill_to"]
126	
127	        resp = dxpy.api.global_workflow_new(dx_hash, **kwargs)
128	        self.set_id(dxid=resp["id"])
129	
130	    def describe(self, fields=None, **kwargs):
131	        '''
132	        :param fields: Hash where the keys are field names that should be returned, and values should be set to True (default is that all fields are returned)
133	        :type fields: dict
134	        :returns: Description of the remote global workflow object
135	        :rtype: dict
136	
137	        Returns a dict with a description of the workflow.
138	
139	        '''
140	        describe_input = {}
141	        if fields:
142	            describe_input['fields'] = fields
143	
144	        if self._dxid is not None:
145	            self._desc = dxpy.api.global_workflow_describe(self._dxid, input_params=describe_input, **kwargs)
146	        else:
147	            self._desc = dxpy.api.global_workflow_describe('globalworkflow-' + self._name, alias=self._alias,
148	                                                           input_params=describe_input, **kwargs)
149	
150	        return self._desc
151	
152	    def publish(self, **kwargs):
153	        """
154	        Publishes the global workflow, so all users can find it and use it on the platform.
155	
156	        The current user must be a developer of the workflow.
157	        """
158	        if self._dxid is not None:
159	            return dxpy.api.global_workflow_publish(self._dxid, **kwargs)
160	        else:
161	            return dxpy.api.global_workflow_publish('globalworkflow-' + self._name, alias=self._alias, **kwargs)
162	
163	    def describe_underlying_workflow(self, region, describe_output=None):
164	        """
165	        :param region: region name
166	        :type region: string
167	        :param describe_output: description of a global workflow
168	        :type describe_output: dict
169	        :returns: object description of a workflow
170	        :rtype: : dict
171	
172	        Returns an object description of an underlying workflow from a given region.
173	        """
174	        assert(describe_output is None or describe_output.get('class', '') == 'globalworkflow')
175	
176	        if region is None:
177	            raise DXError(
178	                'DXGlobalWorkflow: region must be provided to get an underlying workflow')
179	
180	        # Perhaps we have cached it already
181	        if region in self._workflow_desc_by_region:
182	            return self._workflow_desc_by_region[region]
183	
184	        if not describe_output:
185	            describe_output = self.describe()
186	
187	        if region not in describe_output['regionalOptions'].keys():
188	            raise DXError('DXGlobalWorkflow: the global workflow {} is not enabled in region {}'.format(
189	                self.get_id(), region))
190	
191	        underlying_workflow_id = describe_output['regionalOptions'][region]['workflow']
192	        dxworkflow = dxpy.DXWorkflow(underlying_workflow_id)
193	        dxworkflow_desc = dxworkflow.describe()
194	        self._workflow_desc_by_region = dxworkflow_desc
195	        return dxworkflow_desc
196	
197	    def get_underlying_workflow(self, region, describe_output=None):
198	        """
199	        :param region: region name
200	        :type region: string
201	        :param describe_output: description of a global workflow
202	        :type describe_output: dict
203	        :returns: object handler of a workflow
204	        :rtype: :class:`~dxpy.bindings.dxworkflow.DXWorkflow`
205	
206	        Returns an object handler of an underlying workflow from a given region.
207	        """
208	        assert(describe_output is None or describe_output.get('class') == 'globalworkflow')
209	
210	        if region is None:
211	            raise DXError(
212	                'DXGlobalWorkflow: region must be provided to get an underlying workflow')
213	
214	        # Perhaps we have cached it already
215	        if region in self._workflows_by_region:
216	            return self._workflows_by_region[region]
217	
218	        if not describe_output:
219	            describe_output = self.describe()
220	
221	        if region not in describe_output['regionalOptions'].keys():
222	            raise DXError('DXGlobalWorkflow: the global workflow {} is not enabled in region {}'.format(
223	                self.get_id(), region))
224	
225	        underlying_workflow_id = describe_output['regionalOptions'][region]['workflow']
226	        self._workflow_desc_by_region = dxpy.DXWorkflow(underlying_workflow_id)
227	        return dxpy.DXWorkflow(underlying_workflow_id)
228	
229	    def append_underlying_workflow_desc(self, describe_output, region):
230	        """
231	        :param region: region name
232	        :type region: string
233	        :param describe_output: description of a global workflow
234	        :type describe_output: dict
235	        :returns: object description of the global workflow
236	        :rtype: : dict
237	
238	        Appends stages, inputs, outputs and other workflow-specific metadata to a global workflow describe output.
239	
240	        Note: global workflow description does not contain functional metadata (stages, IO), since this data
241	        is region-specific (due to applets and bound inputs) and so reside only in region-specific underlying
242	        workflows. We add them to global_workflow_desc so that it can be used for a workflow or a global workflow
243	        """
244	        assert(describe_output is None or describe_output.get('class') == 'globalworkflow')
245	
246	        underlying_workflow_desc = self.describe_underlying_workflow(region,
247	                                                                     describe_output=describe_output)
248	        for field in ['inputs', 'outputs', 'inputSpec', 'outputSpec', 'stages']:
249	            describe_output[field] = underlying_workflow_desc[field]
250	        return describe_output
251	
252	    def _get_input_name(self, input_str, region=None, describe_output=None):
253	        dxworkflow = self.get_underlying_workflow(region, describe_output=describe_output)
254	        return dxworkflow._get_input_name(input_str)
255	
256	    def _get_run_input(self, workflow_input, project=None, **kwargs):
257	        """
258	        Checks the region in which the global workflow is run
259	        and returns the input associated with the underlying workflow
260	        from that region.
261	        """
262	        region = dxpy.api.project_describe(project,
263	                                           input_params={"fields": {"region": True}})["region"]
264	        dxworkflow = self.get_underlying_workflow(region)
265	        return dxworkflow._get_run_input(workflow_input, project=project, **kwargs)
266	
267	    def _run_impl(self, run_input, **kwargs):
268	        if self._dxid is not None:
269	            return DXAnalysis(dxpy.api.global_workflow_run(self._dxid, input_params=run_input, **kwargs)["id"])
270	        else:
271	            return DXAnalysis(dxpy.api.global_workflow_run('globalworkflow-' + self._name, alias=self._alias,
272	                                                           input_params=run_input,
273	                                                           **kwargs)["id"])
274	
275	    def run(self, workflow_input, *args, **kwargs):
276	        '''
277	        :param workflow_input: Dictionary of the workflow's input arguments; see below for more details
278	        :type workflow_input: dict
279	        :param instance_type: Instance type on which all stages' jobs will be run, or a dict mapping function names to instance types. These may be overridden on a per-stage basis if stage_instance_types is specified.
280	        :type instance_type: string or dict
281	        :param stage_instance_types: A dict mapping stage IDs, names, or indices to either a string (representing an instance type to be used for all functions in that stage), or a dict mapping function names to instance types.
282	        :type stage_instance_types: dict
283	        :param stage_folders: A dict mapping stage IDs, names, indices, and/or the string "*" to folder values to be used for the stages' output folders (use "*" as the default for all unnamed stages)
284	        :type stage_folders: dict
285	        :param rerun_stages: A list of stage IDs, names, indices, and/or the string "*" to indicate which stages should be run even if there are cached executions available
286	        :type rerun_stages: list of strings
287	        :returns: Object handler of the newly created analysis
288	        :rtype: :class:`~dxpy.bindings.dxanalysis.DXAnalysis`
289	
290	        Run the workflow. See :meth:`dxpy.bindings.dxapplet.DXExecutable.run` for additional args.
291	
292	        When providing input for the workflow, keys should be of one of the following forms:
293	
294	        * "N.name" where *N* is the stage number, and *name* is the
295	          name of the input, e.g. "0.reads" if the first stage takes
296	          in an input called "reads"
297	
298	        * "stagename.name" where *stagename* is the stage name, and
299	          *name* is the name of the input within the stage
300	
301	        * "stageID.name" where *stageID* is the stage ID, and *name*
302	          is the name of the input within the stage
303	
304	        * "name" where *name* is the name of a workflow level input
305	          (defined in inputs) or the name that has been
306	          exported for the workflow (this name will appear as a key
307	          in the "inputSpec" of this workflow's description if it has
308	          been exported for this purpose)
309	
310	        '''
311	        return super(DXGlobalWorkflow, self).run(workflow_input, *args, **kwargs)

51	    :type init_from: :class:`~dxpy.bindings.dxworkflow.DXWorkflow`, :class:`~dxpy.bindings.dxanalysis.DXAnalysis`, or string (for analysis IDs only)
52	    :rtype: :class:`DXWorkflow`

54	    Additional optional parameters not listed: all those under
55	    :func:`dxpy.bindings.DXDataObject.new`, except `details`.

57	    Creates a new remote workflow object with project set to *project*
58	    and returns the appropriate handler.

109	        :type workflow_inputs: array of dictionaries

118	        def _set_dx_hash(kwargs, dxhash, key, new_key=None):
119	            new_key = key if new_key is None else new_key
120	            if key in kwargs:
121	                if kwargs[key] is not None:
122	                    dxhash[new_key] = kwargs[key]
123	                del kwargs[key]
124	
125	        if "init_from" in kwargs:
126	            if kwargs["init_from"] is not None:
127	                if not (isinstance(kwargs["init_from"], (DXWorkflow, DXAnalysis)) or \
128	                        (isinstance(kwargs["init_from"], basestring) and \
129	                         re.compile('^analysis-[0-9A-Za-z]{24}$').match(kwargs["init_from"]))):
130	                    raise DXError("Expected init_from to be an instance of DXWorkflow or DXAnalysis, or to be a string analysis ID.")
131	                if isinstance(kwargs["init_from"], basestring):
132	                    dx_hash["initializeFrom"] = {"id": kwargs["init_from"]}
133	                else:
134	                    dx_hash["initializeFrom"] = {"id": kwargs["init_from"].get_id()}
135	                    if isinstance(kwargs["init_from"], DXWorkflow):
136	                        dx_hash["initializeFrom"]["project"] = kwargs["init_from"].get_proj_id()
137	            del kwargs["init_from"]

139	        _set_dx_hash(kwargs, dx_hash, "title")
140	        _set_dx_hash(kwargs, dx_hash, "summary")
141	        _set_dx_hash(kwargs, dx_hash, "description")
142	        _set_dx_hash(kwargs, dx_hash, "output_folder", "outputFolder")
143	        _set_dx_hash(kwargs, dx_hash, "stages")
144	        _set_dx_hash(kwargs, dx_hash, "workflow_inputs", "inputs")

156	    def _get_stage_id(self, stage):
157	        '''
158	        :param stage: A stage ID, name, or index (stage index is the number n for the nth stage, starting from 0; can be provided as an int or a string)
159	        :type stage: int or string
160	        :returns: The stage ID (this is a no-op if it was already a stage ID)
161	        :raises: :class:`~dxpy.exceptions.DXError` if *stage* could not be parsed, resolved to a stage ID, or it could not be found in the workflow
162	        '''
163	        # first, if it is a string, see if it is an integer
164	        if isinstance(stage, basestring):
165	            try:
166	                stage = int(stage)
167	            except:
168	                # we'll try parsing it as a string later
169	                pass
170	
171	        if not isinstance(stage, basestring):
172	            # Try to parse as stage index; ensure that if it's not a
173	            # string that it is an integer at this point.
174	            try:
175	                stage_index = int(stage)
176	            except:
177	                raise DXError('DXWorkflow: the given stage identifier was neither a string stage ID nor an integer index')
178	            if stage_index < 0 or stage_index >= len(self.stages):
179	                raise DXError('DXWorkflow: the workflow contains ' + str(len(self.stages)) + \
180	                              ' stage(s), and the numerical value of the given stage identifier is out of range')
181	            return self.stages[stage_index].get("id")
182	
183	        if re.compile('^([a-zA-Z_]|stage-)[0-9a-zA-Z_]*$').match(stage) is not None:
184	            # Check if there exists a stage with this stage id
185	            stage_id_exists = any([stg['id'] for stg in self.stages if stg.get('id') == stage])
186	            if stage_id_exists:
187	                return stage
188	
189	        # A stage with the provided ID can't be found in the workflow, so look for it as a name
190	        stage_ids_matching_name = [stg['id'] for stg in self.stages if stg.get('name') == stage]
191	        if len(stage_ids_matching_name) == 0:
192	            raise DXError('DXWorkflow: the given stage identifier ' + stage + ' could not be found as a stage ID nor as a stage name')
193	        elif len(stage_ids_matching_name) > 1:
194	            raise DXError('DXWorkflow: more than one workflow stage was found to have the name "' + stage + '"')
195	        else:
196	            return stage_ids_matching_name[0]

198	    def add_stage(self, executable, stage_id=None, name=None, folder=None, stage_input=None, instance_type=None,
199	                  edit_version=None, **kwargs):
200	        '''
201	        :param executable: string or a handler for an app or applet
202	        :type executable: string, DXApplet, or DXApp
203	        :param stage_id: id for the stage (optional)
204	        :type stage_id: string
205	        :param name: name for the stage (optional)
206	        :type name: string
207	        :param folder: default output folder for the stage; either a relative or absolute path (optional)
208	        :type folder: string
209	        :param stage_input: input fields to bind as default inputs for the executable (optional)
210	        :type stage_input: dict
211	        :param instance_type: Default instance type on which all jobs will be run for this stage, or a dict mapping function names to instance type requests
212	        :type instance_type: string or dict
213	        :param edit_version: if provided, the edit version of the workflow that should be modified; if not provided, the current edit version will be used (optional)
214	        :type edit_version: int
215	        :returns: ID of the added stage
216	        :rtype: string
217	        :raises: :class:`~dxpy.exceptions.DXError` if *executable* is not an expected type :class:`~dxpy.exceptions.DXAPIError` for errors thrown from the API call
218	
219	        Adds the specified executable as a new stage in the workflow.
220	        '''
221	        if isinstance(executable, basestring):
222	            exec_id = executable
223	        elif isinstance(executable, DXExecutable):
224	            exec_id = executable.get_id()
225	        else:
226	            raise DXError("dxpy.DXWorkflow.add_stage: executable must be a string or an instance of DXApplet or DXApp")
227	        add_stage_input = {"executable": exec_id}
228	        if stage_id is not None:
229	            add_stage_input["id"] = stage_id
230	        if name is not None:
231	            add_stage_input["name"] = name
232	        if folder is not None:
233	            add_stage_input["folder"] = folder
234	        if stage_input is not None:
235	            add_stage_input["input"] = stage_input
236	        if instance_type is not None:
237	            add_stage_input["systemRequirements"] = SystemRequirementsDict.from_instance_type(instance_type).as_dict()
238	        self._add_edit_version_to_request(add_stage_input, edit_version)
239	        try:
240	            result = dxpy.api.workflow_add_stage(self._dxid, add_stage_input, **kwargs)
241	        finally:
242	            self.describe() # update cached describe
243	        return result['stage']

245	    def get_stage(self, stage, **kwargs):
246	        '''
247	        :param stage: A number for the stage index (for the nth stage, starting from 0), or a string of the stage index, name, or ID
248	        :type stage: int or string
249	        :returns: Hash of stage descriptor in workflow
250	        '''
251	        stage_id = self._get_stage_id(stage)
252	        result = next((stage for stage in self.stages if stage['id'] == stage_id), None)
253	        if result is None:
254	            raise DXError('The stage ID ' + stage_id + ' could not be found')
255	        return result

303	        :param title: workflow title to set; cannot be provided with *unset_title* set to True

442	    def _get_input_name(self, input_str, region=None, describe_output=None):
443	        '''
444	        :param input_str: A string of one of the forms: "<exported input field name>", "<explicit workflow input field name>", "<stage ID>.<input field name>", "<stage index>.<input field name>", "<stage name>.<input field name>"
445	        :type input_str: string
446	        :returns: If the given form was one of those which uses the stage index or stage name, it is translated to the stage ID for use in the API call (stage name takes precedence)
447	        '''
448	        if '.' in input_str:
449	            stage_identifier, input_name = input_str.split('.', 1)
450	            # Try to parse as a stage ID or name
451	            return self._get_stage_id(stage_identifier) + '.' + input_name
452	
453	        return input_str

455	    def _get_effective_input(self, workflow_input):
456	        effective_input = {}
457	        for key in workflow_input:
458	            input_name = self._get_input_name(key)
459	            if input_name in effective_input:
460	                raise DXError('DXWorkflow: the input for ' + input_name + ' was provided more than once')
461	            effective_input[input_name] = workflow_input[key]

464	    def _get_run_input(self, workflow_input, **kwargs):
465	        effective_workflow_input = self._get_effective_input(workflow_input)
466	
467	        run_input = DXExecutable._get_run_input_common_fields(effective_workflow_input, **kwargs)
468	
469	        if kwargs.get('stage_instance_types') is not None:
470	            run_input['stageSystemRequirements'] = {}
471	            for stage, value in kwargs['stage_instance_types'].items():
472	                if stage != '*':
473	                    stage = self._get_stage_id(stage)
474	                run_input['stageSystemRequirements'][stage] = SystemRequirementsDict.from_instance_type(value).as_dict()
475	
476	        if kwargs.get('stage_folders') is not None:
477	            run_input['stageFolders'] = {}
478	            for stage, value in kwargs['stage_folders'].items():
479	                if stage != '*':
480	                    stage = self._get_stage_id(stage)
481	                run_input['stageFolders'][stage] = value
482	
483	        if kwargs.get('rerun_stages') is not None:
484	            run_input['rerunStages'] = [
485	                _stage if _stage == '*' else self._get_stage_id(_stage)
486	                for _stage in kwargs['rerun_stages']
487	            ]
488	
489	        if kwargs.get('ignore_reuse', False):
490	            run_input['ignoreReuse'] = ['*']
491	
492	        if kwargs.get('ignore_reuse_stages') is not None:
493	            run_input['ignoreReuse'] = [
494	                _stage if _stage == '*' else self._get_stage_id(_stage)
495	                for _stage in kwargs['ignore_reuse_stages']
496	            ]

498	        return run_input

503	    def run(self, workflow_input, *args, **kwargs):
504	        '''
505	        :param workflow_input: Dictionary of the workflow's input arguments; see below for more details
506	        :type workflow_input: dict

1	# The taxonomy, in full
2	
3	An **energy smell** is code that spends energy on work the program does not
4	need, and that a specific refactoring can remove without changing what the
5	program does. This taxonomy names them: twelve categories, sixty-five root
6	causes.
7	
8	This page is what to look for in step 1. Read it before you read the code, and
9	keep it beside you: of every function, ask whether any of these is happening
10	there. The **category table** says what each family of waste covers; the
11	**root cause table** below it lists all sixty-five, one line each — enough to
12	recognise one, not enough to decide it. Deciding is step 2, with the root
13	cause's card.
14	
15	Cards live at `reference/categories/<ID>.md` — a category's root causes, with
16	the repair for each — and `reference/root-causes/<ID>.<S>.md`, which open at
17	`step.py done 1`.
18	
19	## Categories
20	
21	| ID | Category | Covers | Card |
22	|---|---|---|---|
23	| **C1** | Redundant Computation | Energy waste from executing work that does not contribute to the program's required output or that leaves program state unchanged | `reference/categories/C1.md` (8) |
24	| **C2** | Unnecessary Call Overhead | Energy waste from extra layers of function calls, method delegation, or dynamic dispatch that add overhead without proportional benefit | `reference/categories/C2.md` (3) |
25	| **C3** | Inefficient Iteration Patterns | Energy waste from loops that perform more per-iteration work than necessary, iterate more times than required, use suboptimal loop constructs, or fail to terminate correctly | `reference/categories/C3.md` (7) |
26	| **C4** | Inefficient Control Flow | Energy waste from branching, conditions, or dispatch logic that performs unnecessary checks, uses suboptimal evaluation order, or employs patterns that prevent interpreter optimization | `reference/categories/C4.md` (8) |
27	| **C5** | Suboptimal Data Structures | Energy waste from choosing, provisioning, or converting data structures that do not match the workload's access pattern or size requirements | `reference/categories/C5.md` (4) |
28	| **C6** | Unnecessary Memory Usage | Patterns that allocate, copy, retain, or leak memory beyond what the workload requires, increasing garbage collection overhead, memory-bus traffic, and system energy consumption | `reference/categories/C6.md` (7) |
29	| **C7** | Suboptimal Algorithmic | Energy waste from choosing an algorithm, decomposition, or computation strategy that explores more of the problem space than necessary or uses higher complexity than the problem requires | `reference/categories/C7.md` (5) |
30	| **C8** | Missing Reuse | Energy waste from failing to store and reuse results of expensive computations, lookups, or data fetches, causing the same work to be repeated across calls, requests, or access sites | `reference/categories/C8.md` (4) |
31	| **C9** | Inefficient External Data Access | Energy waste from inefficient interaction with external systems: databases, file systems, network services, and APIs | `reference/categories/C9.md` (4) |
32	| **C10** | Underused Language Primitives | Energy waste from not using available optimized language features, standard library functions, or runtime-specific constructs that would accomplish the same task more efficiently | `reference/categories/C10.md` (6) |
33	| **C11** | Inefficient Concurrency Management | Energy waste from thread/task misuse, synchronization overhead, contention, or failure to exploit available parallelism | `reference/categories/C11.md` (5) |
34	| **C12** | Poor Hardware Locality Usage | Energy waste driven by CPU and memory hierarchy behavior such as cache misses, branch misprediction, and suboptimal memory access patterns | `reference/categories/C12.md` (4) |
35	
36	## Every root cause, one line each
37	
38	### C1 — Redundant Computation
39	
40	| ID | Name | Looks for |
41	|---|---|---|
42	| **C1.S1** | Dead Code | a value computed and bound to a name that nothing ever reads |
43	| **C1.S2** | Redundant Assignment | a store that leaves the program's state exactly as it already was |
44	| **C1.S3** | Redundant Control Flow | a branch whose outcome is the same whichever way it goes |
45	| **C1.S4** | Repeated Computation | the same value computed twice in one scope, where one local would serve both |
46	| **C1.S5** | Resultless Computation | a computation run in full whose result nothing downstream actually needs |
47	| **C1.S6** | Unnecessary Initialization | setup done unconditionally that only one path actually needs |
48	| **C1.S7** | Unnecessary Variable | a name bound, read exactly once, and never needed again |
49	| **C1.S8** | Excessive Runtime-Management Calls | runtime housekeeping invoked far more often than anything needs it |
50	
51	### C2 — Unnecessary Call Overhead
52	
53	| ID | Name | Looks for |
54	|---|---|---|
55	| **C2.S1** | Unnecessary Method Delegation | a wrapper or property that forwards, adds nothing, and sits on a hot path |
56	| **C2.S2** | Missing Static Declaration | a method that never touches `self` and still pays to be bound to an instance |
57	| **C2.S3** | Excessive Modularization in Hot Path | a chain of thin layers whose frames cost more than the work at the bottom |
58	
59	### C3 — Inefficient Iteration Patterns
60	
61	| ID | Name | Looks for |
62	|---|---|---|
63	| **C3.S1** | Inefficient Iteration Construct | a loop written in a form that does more interpreter work per element than it needs to |
64	| **C3.S2** | Recomputing Loop-Invariant Values | an expression recomputed every iteration whose answer never changes |
65	| **C3.S3** | Inefficient Per-Iteration Setup | an object or resource created once per iteration that the whole loop could share |
66	| **C3.S4** | Inefficient Nested Iteration | an inner loop that searches, where a lookup would turn n*m into n+m |
67	| **C3.S5** | Missing Loop Early Exit | a loop that keeps going after its answer is already settled |
68	| **C3.S6** | Unfiltered Bulk Iteration | the whole collection processed when only a subset was ever wanted |
69	| **C3.S7** | Inefficient Array Mutation in Loop | a collection edited while it is being walked |
70	
71	### C4 — Inefficient Control Flow
72	
73	| ID | Name | Looks for |
74	|---|---|---|
75	| **C4.S1** | Poor Short-Circuit Ordering | a boolean chain that evaluates its expensive operand before the cheap one that usually decides |
76	| **C4.S2** | Redundant Conditional Evaluation | a test whose answer was already settled before it ran |
77	| **C4.S3** | Inefficient Conditional Nesting | a nest or chain of branches that tests more than it has to, where a lookup would test once |
78	| **C4.S4** | Missing Else-If | consecutive `if`s on one subject that are exclusive in fact but not in form |
79	| **C4.S5** | Expensive Comparison | a type check made per element where the answer never varies or the types could dispatch themselves |
80	| **C4.S6** | Expensive Exception Control Flow | an exception used as ordinary control flow, on a path where it is raised often |
81	| **C4.S7** | Missing Edge-Case Guards | a missing cheap test that would let a common trivial input skip the expensive path |
82	| **C4.S8** | Non-Idiomatic Condition | a condition spelled the long way round, missing the interpreter's fast path |
83	
84	### C5 — Suboptimal Data Structures
85	
86	| ID | Name | Looks for |
87	|---|---|---|
88	| **C5.S1** | Inefficient Data Structure Choice | a container whose type makes its most frequent operation the expensive one |
89	| **C5.S2** | Missing Helper Type | a collection searched again and again where one index built beside it would answer every question |
90	| **C5.S3** | Over-Provisioned Data Type | a representation heavier than the data it holds actually requires |
91	| **C5.S4** | Unnecessary Representation Change | a conversion between representations that the code on either side did not need |
92	
93	### C6 — Unnecessary Memory Usage
94	
95	| ID | Name | Looks for |
96	|---|---|---|
97	| **C6.S1** | Unnecessary Object | objects created and thrown away that never needed to exist |
98	| **C6.S2** | Unnecessary Copying | data duplicated when the original could have been used or changed in place |
99	| **C6.S3** | Unnecessary Data Materialization | a whole sequence built in memory when the consumer wanted it one element at a time |
100	| **C6.S4** | Oversized Data Retaining | something long-lived holding far more data than anything later reads |
101	| **C6.S5** | Over-Allocation | capacity reserved up front for data that never arrives |
102	| **C6.S6** | Leaked Resource Handles | a file, socket or connection acquired with nothing guaranteeing its release |
103	| **C6.S7** | Leaking Mutable Default Arguments | a mutable default argument that quietly accumulates across every call |
104	
105	### C7 — Suboptimal Algorithmic
106	
107	| ID | Name | Looks for |
108	|---|---|---|
109	| **C7.S1** | Suboptimal Algorithm Choice | an algorithm of worse complexity than the problem requires |
110	| **C7.S2** | Inefficient Problem Decomposition | a search exploring subproblems it could have pruned, reordered or reused |
111	| **C7.S3** | Avoidable Recursive Implementation | a recursion paying a frame per level where a loop would use one |
112	| **C7.S4** | Inefficient Operation Ordering | two commuting operations in the order that makes the expensive one see more data |
113	| **C7.S5** | Unsimplified Operation | an operation doing more work than an algebraic fact about its inputs requires |
114	
115	### C8 — Missing Reuse
116	
117	| ID | Name | Looks for |
118	|---|---|---|
119	| **C8.S1** | Missing Memoization Cache | a deterministic computation repeated across calls that a cache would answer |
120	| **C8.S2** | Missing Derived-Value Reuse | an expensive artefact derived again on every use instead of once for the process |
121	| **C8.S3** | Missing Local Lookup Caching | a name or attribute chain re-resolved every iteration for a value that never moves |
122	| **C8.S4** | Redundant Data Fetching | the same external data fetched again when the copy in memory was still good |
123	
124	### C9 — Inefficient External Data Access
125	
126	| ID | Name | Looks for |
127	|---|---|---|
128	| **C9.S1** | Fragmented I/O Calls | many small independent external operations where one bulk operation would do |
129	| **C9.S2** | Oversized Data Retrieval | more data pulled across a process boundary than the program ever consults |
130	| **C9.S3** | Inefficient Retrieval Paths | one fetch per row of an earlier fetch, where a join would have taken one trip |
131	| **C9.S4** | Expensive Query Pattern | a query whose shape makes the engine do far more work than the answer needs |
132	
133	### C10 — Underused Language Primitives
134	
135	| ID | Name | Looks for |
136	|---|---|---|
137	| **C10.S1** | Skipping Optimized Built-ins | a hand-written loop doing bulk work a C-level primitive already does |
138	| **C10.S2** | Inefficient Built-in Choice | one primitive used where a cheaper primitive computes the same answer |
139	| **C10.S3** | Missing Bulk Primitive Usage | a per-element call inside a loop that a single batched call would replace |
140	| **C10.S4** | Inefficient String Concatenation | a string grown with `+=` in a loop, where the target is aliased or the parts are many |
141	| **C10.S5** | Inefficient Scope Lookup | a global or builtin re-resolved through the module namespace on every iteration |
142	| **C10.S6** | Expensive Operator Overloads | an operator on a user-defined type dispatching and allocating once per element |
143	
144	### C11 — Inefficient Concurrency Management
145	
146	| ID | Name | Looks for |
147	|---|---|---|
148	| **C11.S1** | Excessive Lock Contention | a lock held across work that shares nothing, serialising what could overlap |
149	| **C11.S2** | Forced Serial Bottleneck | concurrency paid for in full while one shared resource serialises all of it |
150	| **C11.S3** | Leaked Background Threads | workers started and never stopped, accumulating for the life of the process |
151	| **C11.S4** | Blocking The Main Thread | a synchronous blocking call inside a coroutine, stopping every other task |
152	| **C11.S5** | Missed Parallelism Opportunities | independent work run one item at a time when the waits could have overlapped |
153	
154	### C12 — Poor Hardware Locality Usage
155	
156	| ID | Name | Looks for |
157	|---|---|---|
158	| **C12.S1** | Inefficient Large-Stride Traversal | a contiguous buffer traversed against the direction its memory is laid out in |
159	| **C12.S2** | Sparse Element Access | scattered reads into a large buffer, using one element of every cache line fetched |
160	| **C12.S3** | Unpredictable Branches | a data-dependent branch in a compiled hot loop that the CPU cannot predict |
161	| **C12.S4** | Inefficient Array Declaration Order | a declared struct whose field order puts cold data in front of hot data |
162	
163	## Using this well
164	
165	**Any category may apply to any code.** Nothing about a repository rules a
166	category in or out in advance. Work from what the code actually does.
167	
168	**Read the card, not the name, and not the line above.** These names are three
169	or four words long and several of them cover something narrower — or wider —
170	than they sound like. The one-line summaries here are index entries, precise
171	enough to recognise something by and not enough to decide anything from. The
172	card is the claim.
173	
174	**The index tells you what to look for, not what you will find.** A unit goes
175	on your list because of what its code does, not because a line here sounds
176	like it. Finding nothing in a category is a perfectly ordinary outcome.
177	
178	**Cards overlap.** When two root causes both describe what you repaired,
179	either attribution is fine — say which you chose.
180	
181	## What tools can and cannot contribute
182	
183	Any static rule, in any tool, recognises a syntactic shape that somebody
184	described in advance. That makes rules dependable about the shapes they know
185	and completely blind to everything else. Two consequences, and they point in
186	opposite directions:
187	
188	- **A rule firing has observed a pattern, not diagnosed a problem.** Every
189	  pattern in this taxonomy is the right thing to write somewhere, which is what
190	  each card's `Looks like it, but is not` section records.
191	  Some of what any rule reports is therefore wrong here, and saying which is
192	  part of the job.
193	- **A rule staying quiet has observed nothing.** Waste that lives in the
194	  arrangement of a program — work computed and discarded, a data shape that
195	  forces every later step to compensate, a query issued once per row — has no
196	  fixed syntactic shape at all, and is usually the expensive kind.
197	
198	Reading the code is the primary method here. Anything a tool tells you is a
199	second opinion to reconcile with what you already worked out.
200

35	def _upload_file(dir, name, content=None, platform_path=None, wait_until_closed=True):
36	    filep = os.path.join(dir, name)
37	
38	    if content is None:
39	        if IS_WINDOWS:
40	            res = subprocess.run(["fsutil", "file", "createnew", filep, str(FILESIZE * 1024 * 1024)], stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL, stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL)
41	        else:
42	            res = subprocess.run(["dd", "if=/dev/random", "of=%s" % filep, "bs=%d" % (1024 * 1024), "count=%s" % FILESIZE], stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL, stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL)
43	        assert res.returncode == 0
44	    else:
45	        with open(filep, 'w') as fh:
46	            fh.write(content)
47	
48	    cmd = ["dx", "upload", "--brief"]
49	    if platform_path is not None:
50	        cmd += ["--path", platform_path]
51	    cmd += [filep]
52	
53	    res = subprocess.run(cmd, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE, universal_newlines=True)
54	    assert res.returncode == 0
55	    file_id = res.stdout.strip()
56	    assert file_id.startswith("file-")
57	
58	    if wait_until_closed:
59	        for _ in range(20):
60	            res = subprocess.run(["dx", "describe", "--json", file_id], stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE, universal_newlines=True)
61	            if json.loads(res.stdout)["state"] == "closed":
62	                return file_id, filep
63	            time.sleep(10)
64	        raise AssertionError("Files did not reach closed state within a time limit")
65	
66	    return file_id, filep

33	        self.pattern = pattern.split("-")

78	    for pyenv in sorted(test_results.keys()):
79	        code = test_results[pyenv]["code"]
80	        msg = f"  {'[ SUCCESS ]' if code == EXIT_SUCCESS else '[  FAIL   ]'}        {pyenv} (exit code: {code}"
81	        if test_results[pyenv]["failed_tests"] is not None:
82	            msg += ", failed tests: " + ", ".join(test_results[pyenv]["failed_tests"])
83	        msg += ")"
84	        logging.info(msg)
85	
86	    if report_file:
87	        with open(report_file, 'w') as fh:
88	            json.dump(test_results, fh)
89	
90	    return 0 if all(map(lambda x: x["code"] == EXIT_SUCCESS, test_results.values())) else 1
91	
92	
93	def init_logging(verbose: bool) -> None:
94	    logging.basicConfig(format='%(asctime)s - %(levelname)s - %(message)s', level=logging.DEBUG if verbose else logging.INFO)
95	
96	
97	def init_base_argparser(parser) -> None:
98	    parser.add_argument("-d", "--dx-toolkit", required=True, help="Path to dx-toolkit source dir")
99	    parser.add_argument("-b", "--dx-toolkit-ref", help="dx-toolkit git reference (branch, commit, etc.) to test")
100	    parser.add_argument("--pull", action="store_true", help="Pull dx-toolkit repo before running the tests")
101	    parser.add_argument("-t", "--token", required=True, help="API token")
102	    parser.add_argument("-l", "--logs", default="./logs", help="Directory where to store logs")
103	    parser.add_argument("-e", "--env", choices=["stg", "prod"], default="stg", help="Platform")
104	    parser.add_argument("-w", "--workers", type=int, default=1, help="Number of workers (i.e. parallelly running tests)")
105	    parser.add_argument("-a", "--retries", type=int, default=1, help="Number of retries for failed execution to eliminate network issues")
106	    parser.add_argument("-r", "--extra-requirement", dest="extra_requirements", action="append", help="Explicitly install this library to the virtual environment before installing dx-toolkit. Format is the same as requirements.txt file.")
107	    parser.add_argument("-o", "--report", help="Save status report to file in JSON format")
108	    pyenv_group = parser.add_mutually_exclusive_group()
109	    pyenv_group.add_argument("-f", "--pyenv-filter", dest="pyenv_filters", action="append", help="Run only in environments matching the filters. Supported are wild-card character '*' (e.g. ubuntu-*-py3-*) or regular expression (when using --regexp-filters flag). Exclusive filters can be using when prefixed with '!'.")
110	    pyenv_group.add_argument("--run-failed", metavar="REPORT", help="Load report file and run only failed environments")
111	    parser.add_argument("--print-logs", action="store_true", help="Print logs of all executions")
112	    parser.add_argument("--print-failed-logs", action="store_true", help="Print logs of failed executions")
113	    parser.add_argument("--regexp-filters", action="store_true", help="Apply filters as a fully-featured regular expressions")
114	    parser.add_argument("--pytest-matching", help="Run only tests matching given substring expression (the same as pytest -k EXPRESSION)")
115	    parser.add_argument("--pytest-exitfirst", action="store_true", help="Exit pytest instantly on first error or failed test (the same as pytest -x)")
116	    parser.add_argument("--pytest-tee", action="store_true", help="Also print stdout/stderr during execution (the same as pytest --capture=tee-sys)")
117	    parser.add_argument("-v", "--verbose", action="store_true", help="Verbose logging")
118	
119	
120	def filter_pyenvs(all_pyenvs, filters_inclusive, filters_exclusive):
121	    pyenvs = all_pyenvs
122	    if filters_inclusive is not None and len(filters_inclusive) > 0:
123	        pyenvs = [p for p in pyenvs if any(map(lambda x: x.match(p), filters_inclusive))]
124	    if filters_exclusive is not None and len(filters_exclusive) > 0:
125	        pyenvs = [p for p in pyenvs if all(map(lambda x: not x.match(p), filters_exclusive))]
126	
127	    pyenvs.sort()
128	
129	    return pyenvs
130	
131	
132	def parse_common_args(args) -> dict:
133	    pytest_args = []
134	    if args.pytest_matching:
135	        pytest_args += ["-k", args.pytest_matching]
136	    if args.pytest_exitfirst:
137	        pytest_args.append("-x")
138	    if args.pytest_tee:
139	        pytest_args += ["--capture", "tee-sys"]
140	
141	    pyenv_filters_inclusive = None
142	    pyenv_filters_exclusive = None
143	    MatcherClass = RegexpMatcher if args.regexp_filters else WildcardMatcher
144	    if args.run_failed:
145	        with open(args.run_failed) as fh:
146	            pyenv_filters_inclusive = [ExactMatcher(k) for k, v in json.load(fh).items() if v != 0]
147	    elif args.pyenv_filters:
148	        pyenv_filters_inclusive = [MatcherClass(f) for f in args.pyenv_filters if f[0] != "!"]
149	        pyenv_filters_exclusive = [MatcherClass(f[1:]) for f in args.pyenv_filters if f[0] == "!"]
150	
151	    if args.pull:
152	        logging.debug("Pulling dx-toolkit git repository")
153	        try:
154	            subprocess.run(["git", "pull"], cwd=args.dx_toolkit, check=True, capture_output=True)
155	        except:
156	            logging.exception("Unable to pull dx-toolkit git repo")
157	            sys.exit(1)
158	
159	    if args.dx_toolkit_ref:
160	        logging.debug(f"Checking out dx-toolkit git reference '{args.dx_toolkit_ref}'")
161	        try:
162	            subprocess.run(["git", "checkout", args.dx_toolkit_ref], cwd=args.dx_toolkit, check=True, capture_output=True)
163	        except:
164	            logging.exception("Unable to checkout dx-toolkit git reference")
165	            sys.exit(1)
166	
167	    logs_dir = Path(args.logs)
168	    if not logs_dir.is_dir():
169	        logging.debug("Logs directory does not exist. Creating...")
170	        logs_dir.mkdir()
171	
172	    return dict(
173	        dx_toolkit=Path(args.dx_toolkit),
174	        token=args.token,
175	        env=args.env,
176	        pyenv_filters_inclusive=pyenv_filters_inclusive,
177	        pyenv_filters_exclusive=pyenv_filters_exclusive,
178	        extra_requirements=args.extra_requirements,
179	        pytest_args=pytest_args,
180	        report=args.report,
181	        logs_dir=logs_dir,
182	        print_logs=args.print_logs,
183	        print_failed_logs=args.print_failed_logs,
184	        workers=args.workers,
185	        retries=args.retries,
186	    )
