67	def _validate_system_requirements(system_requirements):
68	    """
69	    Validates systemRequirements section of dxapp.json for instanceTypeSelector constraints.
70	
71	    :param system_requirements: The systemRequirements section from runSpec
72	    :type system_requirements: dict
73	    :raises AppBuilderException: If validation fails
74	    """
75	    if not isinstance(system_requirements, dict):
76	        return
77	
78	    for entry_point, requirements in system_requirements.items():
79	        if not isinstance(requirements, dict):
80	            continue
81	
82	        has_instance_type = 'instanceType' in requirements
83	        has_instance_type_selector = 'instanceTypeSelector' in requirements
84	        has_cluster_spec = 'clusterSpec' in requirements
85	
86	        # Check mutual exclusivity: instanceType and instanceTypeSelector
87	        if has_instance_type and has_instance_type_selector:
88	            raise AppBuilderException(
89	                "instanceType and instanceTypeSelector keywords are mutually exclusive "
90	                "in systemRequirements for entry point '{}'".format(entry_point)
91	            )
92	
93	        # Check mutual exclusivity: instanceTypeSelector and clusterSpec
94	        if has_instance_type_selector and has_cluster_spec:
95	            raise AppBuilderException(
96	                "instanceTypeSelector and clusterSpec keywords are mutually exclusive "
97	                "in systemRequirements for entry point '{}'".format(entry_point)
98	            )

145	def build(src_dir, parallel_build=True):
146	    """
147	    Runs any build scripts that are found in the specified directory.
148	
149	    In particular, runs ``./configure`` if it exists, followed by ``make -jN``
150	    if it exists (building with as many parallel tasks as there are CPUs on the
151	    system).
152	    """
153	    # TODO: use Gentoo or deb buildsystem
154	    config_script = os.path.join(src_dir, "configure")
155	    if os.path.isfile(config_script) and os.access(config_script, os.X_OK):
156	        logger.debug("Running ./configure in {cwd}".format(cwd=os.path.abspath(src_dir)))
157	        try:
158	            subprocess.check_call([config_script])
159	        except subprocess.CalledProcessError as e:
160	            raise AppBuilderException("./configure in target directory failed with exit code %d" % (e.returncode,))
161	    if os.path.isfile(os.path.join(src_dir, "Makefile")) \
162	        or os.path.isfile(os.path.join(src_dir, "makefile")) \
163	        or os.path.isfile(os.path.join(src_dir, "GNUmakefile")):
164	        if parallel_build:
165	            make_shortcmd = "make -j%d" % (NUM_CORES,)
166	        else:
167	            make_shortcmd = "make"
168	        logger.debug("Building with {make} in {cwd}".format(make=make_shortcmd, cwd=os.path.abspath(src_dir)))
169	        try:
170	            make_cmd = ["make", "-C", src_dir]
171	            if parallel_build:
172	                make_cmd.append("-j" + str(NUM_CORES))
173	            subprocess.check_call(make_cmd)
174	        except subprocess.CalledProcessError as e:
175	            raise AppBuilderException("%s in target directory failed with exit code %d" % (make_shortcmd, e.returncode))

192	def is_link_local(link_target):
193	    """
194	    :param link_target: The target of a symbolic link, as given by os.readlink()
195	    :type link_target: string
196	    :returns: A boolean indicating the link is local to the current directory.
197	              This is defined to mean that os.path.isabs(link_target) == False
198	              and the link NEVER references the parent directory, so
199	              "./foo/../../curdir/foo" would return False.
200	    :rtype: boolean
201	    """
202	    is_local=(not os.path.isabs(link_target))
203	
204	    if is_local:
205	        # make sure that the path NEVER extends outside the resources directory!
206	        d,l = os.path.split(link_target)
207	        link_parts = []
208	        while l:
209	            link_parts.append(l)
210	            d,l = os.path.split(d)
211	        curr_path = os.sep
212	
213	        for p in reversed(link_parts):
214	            is_local = (is_local and not (curr_path == os.sep and p == os.pardir) )
215	            curr_path = os.path.abspath(os.path.join(curr_path, p))
216	
217	    return is_local

219	def _fix_perms(perm_obj):
220	    """
221	    :param perm_obj: A permissions object, as given by os.stat()
222	    :type perm_obj: integer
223	    :returns: A permissions object that is the result of "chmod a+rX" on the
224	              given permission object.  This is defined to be the permission object
225	              bitwise or-ed with all stat.S_IR*, and if the stat.S_IXUSR bit is
226	              set, then the permission object should also be returned bitwise or-ed
227	              with stat.S_IX* (stat.S_IXUSR not included because it would be redundant).
228	    :rtype: integer
229	    """
230	    ret_perm = perm_obj | stat.S_IROTH | stat.S_IRGRP | stat.S_IRUSR
231	    if ret_perm & stat.S_IXUSR:
232	        ret_perm = ret_perm | stat.S_IXGRP | stat.S_IXOTH
233	
234	    return ret_perm
235	
236	def _fix_perm_filter(tar_obj):
237	    """
238	    :param tar_obj: A TarInfo object to be added to a tar file
239	    :tpye tar_obj: tarfile.TarInfo
240	    :returns: A TarInfo object with permissions changed (a+rX)
241	    :rtype: tarfile.TarInfo
242	    """
243	    tar_obj.mode = _fix_perms(tar_obj.mode)
244	    return tar_obj

247	def upload_resources(src_dir, project=None, folder='/', ensure_upload=False, force_symlinks=False, brief=False, resources_dir=None, worker_resources_subpath=""):
248	    """
249	    :param ensure_upload: If True, will bypass checksum of resources directory
250	                          and upload resources bundle unconditionally;
251	                          will NOT be able to reuse this bundle in future builds.
252	                          Else if False, will compute checksum and upload bundle
253	                          if checksum is different from a previously uploaded
254	                          bundle's checksum.
255	    :type ensure_upload: boolean
256	    :param force_symlinks: If true, will bypass the attempt to dereference any
257	                           non-local symlinks and will unconditionally include
258	                           the link as-is.  Note that this will almost certainly
259	                           result in a broken link within the resource directory
260	                           unless you really know what you're doing.
261	    :type force_symlinks: boolean
262	    :param resources_dir: Directory with resources to be archived and uploaded. If not given, uses `resources/`.
263	    :type resources_dir: str
264	    :param worker_resources_subpath: Path that will be prepended to the default directory where files are extracted on the worker.
265	                                     Default is empty string, therefore files would be extracted directly to the root folder.
266	                                     Example: If "home/dnanexus" is given, files will be extracted into /home/dnanexus.
267	    :type worker_resources_subpath: str
268	    :returns: A list (possibly empty) of references to the generated archive(s)
269	    :rtype: list
270	
271	    If resources_dir exists, archives and uploads the contents of the resources_dir
272	    (usually ``resources/``) subdirectory of *src_dir* to a new remote file
273	    object, and returns a list describing a single bundled dependency in
274	    the form expected by the ``bundledDepends`` field of a run
275	    specification. Returns an empty list, if no archive was created.
276	    """
277	    if not resources_dir:
278	        resources_dir = os.path.join(src_dir, "resources")
279	
280	    applet_spec = _get_applet_spec(src_dir)
281	
282	    if project is None:
283	        dest_project = applet_spec['project']
284	    else:
285	        dest_project = project
286	        applet_spec['project'] = project
287	
288	    if os.path.exists(resources_dir) and len(os.listdir(resources_dir)) > 0:
289	        target_folder = applet_spec['folder'] if 'folder' in applet_spec else folder
290	
291	        # While creating the resource bundle, optimistically look for a
292	        # resource bundle with the same contents, and reuse it if possible.
293	        # The resource bundle carries a property 'resource_bundle_checksum'
294	        # that indicates the checksum; the way in which the checksum is
295	        # computed is given below.   If the checksum matches  (and
296	        # ensure_upload is False), then we will use the existing file,
297	        # otherwise, we will compress and upload the tarball.
298	
299	
300	        # The input to the SHA1 contains entries of the form (whitespace
301	        # only included here for readability):
302	        #
303	        # / \0 MODE \0 MTIME \0
304	        # /foo \0 MODE \0 MTIME \0
305	        # ...
306	        #
307	        # where there is one entry for each directory or file (order is
308	        # specified below), followed by a numeric representation of the
309	        # mode, and the mtime in milliseconds since the epoch.
310	        #
311	        # Note when looking at a link, if the link is to be dereferenced,
312	        # the mtime and mode used are that of the target (using os.stat())
313	        # If the link is to be kept as a link, the mtime and mode are those
314	        # of the link itself (using os.lstat())
315	
316	        with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(suffix=".tar") as tar_tmp_fh:
317	
318	            output_sha1 = hashlib.sha1()
319	            tar_fh = tarfile.open(fileobj=tar_tmp_fh, mode='w')
320	
321	            for dirname, subdirs, files in os.walk(resources_dir):
322	                if not dirname.startswith(resources_dir):
323	                    raise AssertionError('Expected %r to start with root directory %r' % (dirname, resources_dir))
324	
325	                # Add an entry for the directory itself
326	                relative_dirname = dirname[len(resources_dir):]
327	                dir_stat = os.lstat(dirname)
328	                if not relative_dirname.startswith('/'):
329	                    relative_dirname = '/' + relative_dirname
330	
331	                fields = [relative_dirname, str(_fix_perms(dir_stat.st_mode)), str(int(dir_stat.st_mtime * 1000))]
332	                output_sha1.update(b''.join(s.encode('utf-8') + b'\0' for s in fields))
333	
334	                # add an entry in the tar file for the current directory, but
335	                # do not recurse!
336	                tar_fh.add(dirname, arcname=worker_resources_subpath + relative_dirname, recursive=False, filter=_fix_perm_filter)
337	                # Canonicalize the order of subdirectories; this is the order in
338	                # which they will be visited by os.walk
339	                subdirs.sort()
340	
341	                # check the subdirectories for symlinks.  We should throw an error
342	                # if there are any links that point outside of the directory (unless
343	                # --force-symlinks is given).  If a link is pointing internal to
344	                # the directory (or --force-symlinks is given), we should add it
345	                # as a file.
346	                for subdir_name in subdirs:
347	                    dir_path = os.path.join(dirname, subdir_name)
348	
349	                    # If we do have a symlink,
350	                    if os.path.islink(dir_path):
351	                        # Let's get the pointed-to path to ensure that it is
352	                        # still in the directory
353	                        link_target = os.readlink(dir_path)
354	
355	                        # If this is a local link, add it to the list of files (case 1)
356	                        # else raise an error
357	                        if force_symlinks or is_link_local(link_target):
358	                            files.append(subdir_name)
359	                        else:
360	                            raise AppBuilderException("Cannot include symlinks to directories outside of the resource directory.  '%s' points to directory '%s'" % (dir_path, os.path.realpath(dir_path)))
361	
362	
363	                # Canonicalize the order of files so that we compute the
364	                # checksum in a consistent order
365	                for filename in sorted(files):
366	                    deref_link = False
367	
368	                    relative_filename = os.path.join(relative_dirname, filename)
369	                    true_filename = os.path.join(dirname, filename)
370	
371	                    file_stat = os.lstat(true_filename)
372	                    # check for a link here, please!
373	                    if os.path.islink(true_filename):
374	
375	                        # Get the pointed-to path
376	                        link_target = os.readlink(true_filename)
377	
378	                        if not (force_symlinks or is_link_local(link_target)):
379	                            # if we are pointing outside of the directory, then:
380	                            # try to get the true stat of the file and make sure
381	                            # to dereference the link!
382	                            try:
383	                                file_stat = os.stat(os.path.join(dirname, link_target))
384	                                deref_link = True
385	                            except OSError:
386	                                # uh-oh! looks like we have a broken link!
387	                                # since this is guaranteed to cause problems (and
388	                                # we know we're not forcing symlinks here), we
389	                                # should throw an error
390	                                raise AppBuilderException("Broken symlink: Link '%s' points to '%s', which does not exist" % (true_filename, os.path.realpath(true_filename)) )
391	
392	
393	                    fields = [relative_filename, str(_fix_perms(file_stat.st_mode)), str(int(file_stat.st_mtime * 1000))]
394	                    output_sha1.update(b''.join(s.encode('utf-8') + b'\0' for s in fields))
395	
396	                    # If we are to dereference, use the target fn
397	                    if deref_link:
398	                        true_filename = os.path.realpath(true_filename)
399	                    tar_fh.add(true_filename, arcname=worker_resources_subpath + relative_filename, filter=_fix_perm_filter)
400	                # end for filename in sorted(files)
401	
402	            # end for dirname, subdirs, files in os.walk(resources_dir):
403	
404	            # at this point, the tar is complete, so close the tar_fh
405	            tar_fh.close()
406	
407	            # Optimistically look for a resource bundle with the same
408	            # contents, and reuse it if possible. The resource bundle
409	            # carries a property 'resource_bundle_checksum' that indicates
410	            # the checksum; the way in which the checksum is computed is
411	            # given in the documentation of _directory_checksum.
412	
413	            if ensure_upload:
414	                properties_dict = {}
415	                existing_resources = False
416	            else:
417	                directory_checksum = output_sha1.hexdigest()
418	                properties_dict = dict(resource_bundle_checksum=directory_checksum)
419	                existing_resources = dxpy.find_one_data_object(
420	                    project=dest_project,
421	                    folder=target_folder,
422	                    properties=dict(resource_bundle_checksum=directory_checksum),
423	                    visibility='either',
424	                    zero_ok=True,
425	                    state='closed',
426	                    return_handler=True
427	                )
428	
429	            if existing_resources:
430	                if not brief:
431	                    logger.info("Found existing resource bundle that matches local resources directory: " +
432	                                existing_resources.get_id())
433	
434	                dx_resource_archive = existing_resources
435	            else:
436	
437	                logger.debug("Uploading in " + src_dir)
438	                # We need to compress the tar that we've created
439	
440	
441	                targz_fh = tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(suffix=".tar.gz", delete=False)
442	
443	                # compress the file by reading the tar file and passing
444	                # it though a GzipFile object, writing the given
445	                # block size (by default 8192 bytes) at a time
446	                targz_gzf = gzip.GzipFile(fileobj=targz_fh, mode='wb')
447	                tar_tmp_fh.seek(0)
448	                dat = tar_tmp_fh.read(io.DEFAULT_BUFFER_SIZE)
449	                while dat:
450	                    targz_gzf.write(dat)
451	                    dat = tar_tmp_fh.read(io.DEFAULT_BUFFER_SIZE)
452	
453	                targz_gzf.flush()
454	                targz_gzf.close()
455	                targz_fh.close()
456	
457	                if 'folder' in applet_spec:
458	                    try:
459	                        dxpy.get_handler(dest_project).new_folder(applet_spec['folder'], parents=True)
460	                    except dxpy.exceptions.DXAPIError:
461	                        pass # TODO: make this better
462	
463	                dx_resource_archive = dxpy.upload_local_file(
464	                    targz_fh.name,
465	                    wait_on_close=True,
466	                    project=dest_project,
467	                    folder=target_folder,
468	                    hidden=True,
469	                    properties=properties_dict
470	                )
471	
472	                os.unlink(targz_fh.name)
473	
474	                # end compressed file creation and upload
475	
476	            archive_link = dxpy.dxlink(dx_resource_archive.get_id())
477	
478	        # end tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(suffix=".tar") as tar_fh
479	
480	        return [{'name': 'resources.tar.gz', 'id': archive_link}]
481	    else:
482	        return []

485	def upload_applet(src_dir, uploaded_resources, check_name_collisions=True, overwrite=False, archive=False,
486	                  project=None, override_folder=None, override_name=None,
487	                  dry_run=False, brief=False, **kwargs):
488	    """
489	    Creates a new applet object.
490	
491	    :param project: ID of container in which to create the applet.
492	    :type project: str, or None to use whatever is specified in dxapp.json
493	    :param override_folder: folder name for the resulting applet which, if specified, overrides that given in dxapp.json
494	    :type override_folder: str
495	    :param override_name: name for the resulting applet which, if specified, overrides that given in dxapp.json
496	    :type override_name: str
497	
498	    """
499	    applet_spec = _get_applet_spec(src_dir)
500	
501	    if project is None:
502	        dest_project = applet_spec['project']
503	    else:
504	        dest_project = project
505	        applet_spec['project'] = project
506	
507	    if 'name' not in applet_spec:
508	        try:
509	            applet_spec['name'] = os.path.basename(os.path.abspath(src_dir))
510	        except:
511	            raise AppBuilderException("Could not determine applet name from the specification (dxapp.json) or from the name of the working directory (%r)" % (src_dir,))
512	
513	    if override_folder:
514	        applet_spec['folder'] = override_folder
515	    if 'folder' not in applet_spec:
516	        applet_spec['folder'] = '/'
517	
518	    if override_name:
519	        applet_spec['name'] = override_name
520	
521	    if 'dxapi' not in applet_spec:
522	        applet_spec['dxapi'] = dxpy.API_VERSION
523	
524	    applets_to_overwrite = []
525	    archived_applet = None
526	    if check_name_collisions and not dry_run:

699	def _create_or_update_version(app_name, version, app_spec, try_update=True):
700	    """
701	    Creates a new version of the app. Returns an app_id, or None if the app has
702	    already been created and published.
703	    """
704	    # This has a race condition since the app could have been created or
705	    # published since we last looked.
706	    try:
707	        app_id = dxpy.api.app_new(app_spec)["id"]
708	        return app_id
709	    except dxpy.exceptions.DXAPIError as e:
710	        # TODO: detect this error more reliably
711	        if e.name == 'InvalidInput' and e.msg == 'Specified name and version conflict with an existing alias':
712	            print('App %s/%s already exists' % (app_spec["name"], version), file=sys.stderr)
713	            # The version number was already taken, so app/new doesn't work.
714	            # However, maybe it hasn't been published yet, so we might be able
715	            # to app-xxxx/update it.
716	            app_describe = dxpy.api.app_describe("app-" + app_name, alias=version)
717	            if app_describe.get("published", 0) > 0:
718	                return None
719	            return _update_version(app_name, version, app_spec, try_update=try_update)
720	        raise e

722	def _update_version(app_name, version, app_spec, try_update=True):
723	    """
724	    Updates a version of the app in place. Returns an app_id, or None if the
725	    app has already been published.
726	    """
727	    if not try_update:
728	        return None
729	    try:
730	        app_id = dxpy.api.app_update("app-" + app_name, version, app_spec)["id"]
731	        return app_id
732	    except dxpy.exceptions.DXAPIError as e:
733	        if e.name == 'InvalidState':
734	            print('App %s/%s has already been published' % (app_spec["name"], version), file=sys.stderr)
735	            return None
736	        raise e

53	def _fetch_spec_from_dxworkflowjson(src_dir, json_file_name, parser):
54	    """
55	    Returns the parsed contents of a json specification.
56	    Raises WorkflowBuilderException (exit code 3) if this cannot be done.
57	    """
58	    if not os.path.isdir(src_dir):
59	        parser.error("{} is not a directory".format(src_dir))
60	
61	    if not os.path.exists(os.path.join(src_dir, json_file_name)):
62	        raise WorkflowBuilderException(
63	            "Directory {} does not contain dxworkflow.json: not a valid DNAnexus workflow source directory"
64	            .format(src_dir))
65	
66	    with open(os.path.join(src_dir, json_file_name)) as desc:
67	        try:
68	            return json_load_raise_on_duplicates(desc)
69	        except Exception as e:
70	            raise WorkflowBuilderException("Could not parse {} file as JSON: {}".format(json_file_name, e.args))
71	
72	def _cleanup_empty_keys(json_spec):
73	    import re
74	    clean_json = re.sub('\"\w*\": (null|\{\}|\"\"|\[\])(\,|)\s*','',json.dumps(json_spec)).replace(", }","}")
75	    return json.loads(clean_json)

77	def _check_dxcompiler_version(json_spec):
78	    SUPPORTED_DXCOMPILER_VERSION = "2.8.0"
79	    try:
80	        from distutils.version import StrictVersion as Version
81	    except ImportError:
82	        from .utils.version import Version
83	    if json_spec.get("details") and json_spec["details"].get("version"):
84	        compiler_version_used = str(json_spec["details"].get("version"))

309	    /workflow/new API or /globalworkflow/new request.
310	    """
311	    if not json_spec:
312	        return
313	    if not args:
314	        return
315	
316	    validated_spec = copy.deepcopy(json_spec)
317	
318	    # print ignored keys if present in json_spec
319	    unsupported_keys = _get_unsupported_keys(validated_spec.keys(), SUPPORTED_KEYS)
320	    if len(unsupported_keys) > 0:
321	        logger.warn(

323	                .format(", ".join(unsupported_keys)))

376	def _assert_executable_regions_match(workflow_enabled_regions, workflow_spec):
377	    """
378	    Check if the dependent apps/applets/subworkflows in the workflow are enabled in requested regions
379	    Returns the subset of requested regions where all the dependent executables are enabled
380	    If the workflow contains any applets, then the workflow can be currently enabled
381	    in only one region - the region in which the applets are stored.
382	    """
383	    if not workflow_enabled_regions: # empty set
384	        return workflow_enabled_regions
385	    
386	    # get executable from all stages and sort them in the order app/applet/globalworkflow/workflow
387	    executables = sorted([i.get("executable") for i in workflow_spec.get("stages")])
388	
389	    for exect in executables:
390	        if exect.startswith("applet-"):
391	            applet_project = dxpy.DXApplet(exect).project
392	            applet_region = dxpy.DXProject(applet_project).region
393	            if {applet_region} != workflow_enabled_regions:                
394	                raise WorkflowBuilderException("The applet {} is not available in all requested region(s) {}"
395	                                               .format(exect, ','.join(workflow_enabled_regions)))
396	
397	        elif exect.startswith("app-"):
398	            app_regional_options = dxpy.api.app_describe(exect, input_params={"fields": {"regionalOptions": True}})
399	            app_regions = set(app_regional_options['regionalOptions'].keys())
400	            if not workflow_enabled_regions.issubset(app_regions):
401	                additional_workflow_regions = workflow_enabled_regions.difference(app_regions)
402	                mesg = "The app {} is enabled in regions {} while the global workflow in {}.".format(
403	                    exect, ", ".join(app_regions), ", ".join(workflow_enabled_regions))
404	                mesg += " The workflow will not be able to run in {}.".format(", ".join(additional_workflow_regions))
405	                mesg += " If you are a developer of the app, you can enable the app in {} to run the workflow in that region(s).".format(
406	                    ", ".join(additional_workflow_regions))
407	                logger.warn(mesg)
408	                workflow_enabled_regions.intersection_update(app_regions)
409	
410	        elif exect.startswith("workflow-"):
411	             # We recurse to check the regions of the executables of the inner workflow
412	            inner_workflow_spec = dxpy.api.workflow_describe(exect)
413	            workflow_enabled_regions = _assert_executable_regions_match(workflow_enabled_regions, inner_workflow_spec)
414	
415	        elif exect.startswith("globalworkflow-"):
416	            raise WorkflowBuilderException("Building a global workflow with nested global workflows is not yet supported")
417	
418	    return workflow_enabled_regions

430	def _get_validated_enabled_regions(json_spec, args):
431	    """
432	    Returns a set of regions (region names) in which the global workflow
433	    should be enabled. 
434	    
435	    1. validates and synchronizes the regions passed via CLI argument and in the regionalOptions field.
436	    2. checks if these regions are included in the permitted regions of the bill_to
437	    3. checks if the dependencies in all the stages are enabled in these regions
438	    """
439	    # Determine in which regions the global workflow are requested to be available
440	    enabled_regions = dxpy.executable_builder.get_enabled_regions('globalworkflow',
441	                                                                  json_spec,
442	                                                                  args.region,
443	                                                                  WorkflowBuilderException)
444	    if not enabled_regions:
445	        enabled_regions = []
446	        if not dxpy.PROJECT_CONTEXT_ID:
447	            msg = "A context project must be selected to enable a workflow in the project's region."
448	            msg += " You can use 'dx select' to select a project. Otherwise you can use --region option"
449	            msg += " to select a region in which the workflow should be enabled"
450	            raise(WorkflowBuilderException(msg))
451	        current_selected_region = dxpy.api.project_describe(dxpy.PROJECT_CONTEXT_ID,
452	                                           input_params={"fields": {"region": True}})["region"]
453	
454	        enabled_regions.append(current_selected_region)
455	
456	    # Get billable regions
457	    enabled_regions = set(enabled_regions)
458	    billable_regions = dxpy.executable_builder.get_permitted_regions(
459	        json_spec["billTo"], WorkflowBuilderException)
460	    if not enabled_regions.issubset(billable_regions):
461	        raise WorkflowBuilderException("The global workflow cannot be enabled in regions {}, which are not among the permittedRegions of the billTo."
462	                                       .format(",".join(enabled_regions.difference(billable_regions))))
463	
464	    # Verify dependencies in all the stages are also enabled in these regions
465	    enabled_regions = _assert_executable_regions_match(enabled_regions, json_spec)
466	    
467	    if not enabled_regions:
468	        raise AssertionError("This workflow should be enabled in at least one region.")
469	
470	    return enabled_regions

473	def _create_temporary_projects(enabled_regions, bill_to):
474	    """
475	    Creates a temporary project needed to build an underlying workflow
476	    for a global workflow. Returns a dictionary with region names as keys
477	    and project IDs as values
478	
479	    The regions in which projects will be created can be:
480	    i. regions specified in the dxworkflow.json/source workflow spec "regionalOptions"
481	    ii. regions specified as the argument "--region" when calling "dx build"
482	    iii. current context project, if none of the above are set
483	    iv. the regions where dependent applets/apps/workflows are enabled
484	    """
485	    # Create one temp project in each region
486	    projects_by_region = {}  # Project IDs by region
487	    for region in enabled_regions:
488	        try:
489	            project_input = {"name": "Temporary build project for dx build global workflow",
490	                             "region": region,
491	                             "billTo": bill_to}
492	            temp_project = dxpy.api.project_new(project_input)["id"]
493	            projects_by_region[region] = temp_project
494	            logger.debug("Created temporary project {} to build in".format(temp_project))
495	        except:
496	            # Clean up any temp projects that might have been created
497	            if projects_by_region:
498	                dxpy.executable_builder.delete_temporary_projects(projects_by_region.values())
499	            err_exit()
500	    return projects_by_region

504	    """
505	    Creates a workflow in a temporary project for each enabled region.
506	    Returns a tuple of dictionaries: workflow IDs by region and project IDs by region.
507	    The caller is responsible for destroying the projects if this method returns properly.
508	    """
509	    projects_by_region = _create_temporary_projects(enabled_regions, json_spec["billTo"])
510	    workflows_by_region = {}

520	            workflows_by_region[region] = workflow_id
521	    except:
522	        # Clean up
523	        if projects_by_region:
524	            dxpy.executable_builder.delete_temporary_projects(projects_by_region.values())

530	def _build_global_workflow(json_spec, enabled_regions, args):
531	    """
532	    Creates a workflow in a temporary project for each enabled region
533	    and builds a global workflow on the platform based on these workflows.
534	    """
535	    workflows_by_region, projects_by_region = {}, {}  # IDs by region
536	    try:
537	        # prepare "regionalOptions" field for the globalworkflow/new input
538	        existing_regional_options = json_spec.get('regionalOptions', {})
539	
540	        if existing_regional_options:
541	            if set(existing_regional_options.keys()) != set(enabled_regions):
542	                raise WorkflowBuilderException("These enabled regions do have regional options specified \
543	                                           in the JSON spec or from --extra-args: {}",
544	                                           ",".join(set(enabled_regions).difference(set(existing_regional_options.keys()))))
545	                
546	            updated_regional_options= copy.deepcopy(existing_regional_options)
547	        else:
548	            updated_regional_options = dict.fromkeys(enabled_regions, {})
549	        
550	        workflows_by_region, projects_by_region = \
551	            _build_underlying_workflows(enabled_regions, json_spec, args)
552	        for region, workflow_id in workflows_by_region.items():
553	            updated_regional_options[region]["workflow"] = workflow_id
554	
555	        # update existing regionalOptions with underlying workflow ids and ignore regions that are not enabled
556	        json_spec.update({'regionalOptions': updated_regional_options})
557	
558	        # leave only fields that are actually used to build the workflow
559	        gwf_provided_keys = GLOBALWF_SUPPORTED_KEYS.intersection(set(json_spec.keys()))
560	        gwf_final_json = dict((k, v) for k, v in json_spec.items() if k in gwf_provided_keys)
561	
562	        # we don't want to print the whole documentation to the screen so we'll remove these fields
563	        print_spec = copy.deepcopy(gwf_final_json)
564	        if "description" in gwf_final_json:
565	            del print_spec["description"]
566	        if "developerNotes" in gwf_final_json:
567	            del print_spec["developerNotes"]
568	        logger.info("Will create global workflow with spec: {}".format(json.dumps(print_spec)))
569	
570	        # Create a new global workflow version on the platform
571	        global_workflow_id = dxpy.api.global_workflow_new(gwf_final_json)["id"]
572	
573	        logger.info("Uploaded global workflow {n}/{v} successfully".format(n=gwf_final_json["name"],
574	                                                                           v=gwf_final_json["version"]))
575	        logger.info("You can publish this workflow with:")
576	        logger.info("  dx publish {n}/{v}".format(n=gwf_final_json["name"],
577	                                                  v=gwf_final_json["version"]))
578	    finally:
579	        # Clean up
580	        if projects_by_region:
581	            dxpy.executable_builder.delete_temporary_projects(projects_by_region.values())
582	
583	    # Set any additional fields on the created workflow
584	    try:
585	        _set_categories_on_workflow(global_workflow_id, gwf_final_json.get("categories", []))
586	    except:
587	        logger.warn(
588	            "The workflow {n}/{v} was created but setting categories failed".format(n=gwf_final_json['name'],
589	                                                                                    v=gwf_final_json['version']))
590	        raise
591	
592	    return global_workflow_id

645	        if args.mode == 'workflow':
646	            json_spec = _fetch_spec_from_dxworkflowjson(args.src_dir, "dxworkflow.json", parser)

58	    # [PROJECT]:
59	    # [PROJECT]:/FOLDER/
60	    # [PROJECT]:/ENTITYNAME
61	    # [PROJECT]:/FOLDER/ENTITYNAME
62	    return try_call(resolve_path, dest_str)

101	def get_valid_bill_to(bill_to, executable_builder_exception):
102	    """
103	    Check if the requesting user can perform billable activities on behalf of the billTo
104	    If not specified, default to the billTo of the requesting user
105	    otherwise it must be either the ID of the requesting user, 
106	    or an org of which the requesting user is a member with 'allowBillableActivities' permission
107	    """
108	    user_id = dxpy.whoami()
109	    if not bill_to:
110	        return dxpy.api.user_describe(user_id)['billTo']
111	
112	    exception_msg = None
113	    if bill_to.startswith('user-') and bill_to != user_id:
114	        exception_msg = 'Cannot request another user to be the "billTo"'
115	    elif bill_to.startswith('org-'):
116	        try:
117	            member_access = dxpy.api.org_describe(bill_to)
118	            if not member_access['allowBillableActivities']:
119	                exception_msg='You are not a member in {} with allowBillableActivities permission. Please check the billing policy of the org.'.format(bill_to)
120	        except:
121	            exception_msg='Cannot retrieve billing information for {}. Please check your access level and the billing policy of the org.'.format(bill_to)
122	    else:
123	        exception_msg='The field "billTo" must be a valid ID of a user/org.'
124	    
125	    if exception_msg:
126	        raise executable_builder_exception(exception_msg)
127	    
128	    return bill_to

130	def verify_developer_rights(prefixed_name):
131	    """
132	    Checks if the current user is a developer of the app or global workflow
133	    with the given name. If the app/global workflow exists and the user has
134	    developer rights to it, the function returns a named tuple representing
135	    the executable that was queried.
136	    """
137	    assert(prefixed_name.startswith('app-') or prefixed_name.startswith('globalworkflow-'))
138	
139	    if prefixed_name.partition('-')[0] == 'app':
140	        exception_type = dxpy.app_builder.AppBuilderException
141	        describe_method = dxpy.api.app_describe
142	        exception_msg = \
143	            'An app with the given name already exists and you are not a developer of that app'
144	    else:
145	        exception_type = dxpy.workflow_builder.WorkflowBuilderException
146	        describe_method = dxpy.api.global_workflow_describe
147	        exception_msg = \
148	            'A global workflow with the given name already exists and you are not a developer of that workflow'
149	    
150	    name_already_exists = True
151	    is_developer = False
152	    version = None
153	    executable_id = None
154	    FoundExecutable = collections.namedtuple('FoundExecutable', ['name', 'version', 'id'])
155	    try:
156	        describe_output = describe_method(prefixed_name,
157	                                          input_params={"fields": {"isDeveloperFor": True,
158	                                                                   "version": True,
159	                                                                   "id": True}})
160	        is_developer = describe_output['isDeveloperFor']
161	        version = describe_output['version']
162	        executable_id = describe_output['id']
163	    except dxpy.exceptions.DXAPIError as e:
164	        if e.name == 'ResourceNotFound':
165	            name_already_exists = False
166	        elif e.name == 'PermissionDenied':
167	            raise exception_type(exception_msg)
168	        else:
169	            raise e
170	
171	    if not name_already_exists:
172	        # This app/workflow doesn't exist yet so its creation will succeed
173	        # (or at least, not fail on the basis of the ACL).
174	        return FoundExecutable(name=None, version=None, id=None)
175	
176	    name_without_prefix = prefixed_name.partition('-')[2]
177	    if not is_developer:
178	        raise exception_type('You are not a developer for {n}'.format(n=name_without_prefix))
179	
180	    return FoundExecutable(name=name_without_prefix, version=version, id=executable_id)

194	def assert_consistent_reg_options(exec_type, json_spec, executable_builder_exception):
195	    """
196	    Validates the "regionalOptions" field and verifies all the regions used
197	    in "regionalOptions" have the same options.
198	    """
199	    reg_options_spec = json_spec.get('regionalOptions')
200	    json_fn = 'dxapp.json or --extra-args' if exec_type == 'app' else 'dxworkflow.json or --extra-args'
201	
202	    if not isinstance(reg_options_spec, dict):
203	        raise executable_builder_exception("The field 'regionalOptions' in  must be a mapping")
204	    if not reg_options_spec:
205	        raise executable_builder_exception(
206	            "The field 'regionalOptions' in " + json_fn + " must be a non-empty mapping")
207	    regional_options_list = list(reg_options_spec.items())
208	    for region, opts_for_region in regional_options_list:
209	        if not isinstance(opts_for_region, dict):
210	            raise executable_builder_exception("The field 'regionalOptions['" + region +
211	                            "']' in " + json_fn + " must be a mapping")
212	        if set(opts_for_region.keys()) != set(regional_options_list[0][1].keys()):
213	            if set(opts_for_region.keys()) - set(regional_options_list[0][1].keys()):
214	                with_key, without_key = region, regional_options_list[0][0]
215	                key_name = next(iter(set(opts_for_region.keys()) - set(regional_options_list[0][1].keys())))
216	            else:
217	                with_key, without_key = regional_options_list[0][0], region
218	                key_name = next(iter(set(regional_options_list[0][1].keys()) - set(opts_for_region.keys())))
219	            raise executable_builder_exception(
220	                "All regions in regionalOptions must specify the same options; " +
221	                "{} was given for {} but not for {}" .format (key_name, with_key, without_key)
222	            )
223	
224	        if exec_type == 'app':
225	            for key in opts_for_region:
226	                if key in json_spec.get('runSpec', {}):
227	                    raise executable_builder_exception(
228	                    key + " cannot be given in both runSpec and in regional options for " + region)

48	class AssetBuilderException(Exception):
49	    """
50	    This exception is raised by the methods in this module
51	    when asset building fails.
52	    """
53	    pass

55	
56	def parse_asset_spec(src_dir):
57	    if not os.path.isdir(src_dir):
58	        err_exit(src_dir + " is not a valid directory.")
59	    if not os.path.exists(os.path.join(src_dir, "dxasset.json")):
60	        raise AssetBuilderException("'" + src_dir + "' is not a valid DNAnexus asset source directory." +
61	                                    " It does not contain a 'dxasset.json' file.")
62	    with open(os.path.join(src_dir, "dxasset.json")) as asset_desc:
63	        try:
64	            return json_load_raise_on_duplicates(asset_desc)
65	        except Exception as e:
66	            raise AssetBuilderException("Could not parse dxasset.json file as JSON: " + str(e.args))
67	
68	
69	def validate_conf(asset_conf):
70	    """
71	    Validates the contents of the conf file and makes sure that the required information
72	    is provided.
73	        {
74	            "name": "asset_library_name",
75	            "title": "A human readable name",
76	            "description": " A detailed description abput the asset",
77	            "version": "0.0.1",
78	            "runSpecVersion": "1",
79	            "release": "16.04",
80	            "distribution": "Ubuntu"
81	            "execDepends":
82	                        [
83	                            {"name": "samtools", "package_manager": "apt"},
84	                            {"name": "bamtools"},
85	                            {"name": "bio", "package_manager": "gem", "version": "1.4.3"},
86	                            {"name": "pysam","package_manager": "pip", "version": "0.7.4"},
87	                            {"name": "Bio::SeqIO", "package_manager": "cpan", "version": "1.006924"}
88	                        ]
89	        }
90	    """
91	    if 'name' not in asset_conf:
92	        raise AssetBuilderException('The asset configuration does not contain the required field "name".')
93	
94	    # Validate runSpec
95	    if 'release' not in asset_conf or asset_conf['release'] not in ["24.04", "20.04", "16.04", "14.04", "12.04"]:
96	        raise AssetBuilderException('The "release" field value should be either "24.04", "20.04", "16.04" (DEPRECATED), "14.04" (DEPRECATED), or "12.04" (DEPRECATED)')
97	    if 'runSpecVersion' in asset_conf:
98	        if asset_conf['runSpecVersion'] not in ["0", "1"]:
99	            raise AssetBuilderException('The "runSpecVersion" field should be either "0", or "1"')
100	        if (asset_conf['runSpecVersion'] == "1" and asset_conf['release'] != "16.04"):
101	            raise AssetBuilderException('The "runSpecVersion" field can only be "1" if "release" is "16.04"')
102	    else:
103	        asset_conf['runSpecVersion'] = "0"
104	    if 'distribution' in asset_conf:
105	        if asset_conf['distribution'] != "Ubuntu":
106	            raise AssetBuilderException('The distribution may only take the value "Ubuntu".')
107	    else:
108	        asset_conf['distribution'] = "Ubuntu"
109	
110	    if 'version' not in asset_conf:
111	        raise AssetBuilderException('The asset configuration does not contain the required field "version". ')
112	    if 'title' not in asset_conf:
113	        raise AssetBuilderException('The asset configuration does not contain the required field "title". ')
114	    if 'description' not in asset_conf:
115	        raise AssetBuilderException('The asset configuration does not contain the required field "description".')

119	def dx_upload(file_name, dest_project, target_folder, json_out):
120	    try:
121	        maybe_progress_kwargs = {} if json_out else dict(show_progress=True)
122	        remote_file = dxpy.upload_local_file(file_name,
123	                                             project=dest_project,
124	                                             folder=target_folder,
125	                                             wait_on_close=True,
126	                                             **maybe_progress_kwargs)
127	        return remote_file
128	    except:
129	        print("Failed to upload the file " + file_name, file=sys.stderr)
130	        raise

133	def get_asset_make(src_dir, dest_folder, target_folder, json_out):
134	    if os.path.exists(os.path.join(src_dir, "Makefile")):
135	        return dx_upload(os.path.join(src_dir, "Makefile"), dest_folder, target_folder, json_out)
136	    elif os.path.exists(os.path.join(src_dir, "makefile")):
137	        return dx_upload(os.path.join(src_dir, "makefile"), dest_folder, target_folder, json_out)
138	
139	
140	def parse_destination(dest_str):
141	    """
142	    Parses dest_str, which is (roughly) of the form
143	    PROJECT:/FOLDER/NAME, and returns a tuple (project, folder, name)
144	    """
145	    # Interpret strings of form "project-XXXX" (no colon) as project. If
146	    # we pass these through to resolve_path they would get interpreted
147	    # as folder names...
148	    if is_container_id(dest_str):
149	        return (dest_str, None, None)
150	
151	    # ...otherwise, defer to resolver.resolve_path. This handles the
152	    # following forms:
153	    #
154	    # /FOLDER/
155	    # /ENTITYNAME
156	    # /FOLDER/ENTITYNAME
157	    # [PROJECT]:
158	    # [PROJECT]:/FOLDER/
159	    # [PROJECT]:/ENTITYNAME
160	    # [PROJECT]:/FOLDER/ENTITYNAME
161	    return try_call(resolve_path, dest_str)
162	
163	
164	def get_asset_tarball(asset_name, src_dir, dest_project, dest_folder, json_out):
165	    """
166	    If the src_dir contains a "resources" directory its contents are archived and
167	    the archived file is uploaded to the platform
168	    """
169	    if os.path.isdir(os.path.join(src_dir, "resources")):
170	        temp_dir = tempfile.mkdtemp()
171	        try:
172	            resource_file = os.path.join(temp_dir, asset_name + "_resources.tar.gz")
173	            cmd = ["tar", "-czf", resource_file, "-C", os.path.join(src_dir, "resources"), "."]
174	            subprocess.check_call(cmd)
175	            file_id = dx_upload(resource_file, dest_project, dest_folder, json_out)
176	            return file_id
177	        finally:
178	            shutil.rmtree(temp_dir)

181	def build_asset(args):
182	    if args.src_dir is None:
183	        args.src_dir = os.getcwd()
184	
185	    dest_project_name = None
186	    dest_folder_name = None
187	    dest_asset_name = None
188	    make_file = None
189	    asset_file = None
190	    conf_file = None
191	
192	    try:
193	        asset_conf = parse_asset_spec(args.src_dir)
194	        validate_conf(asset_conf)
195	        asset_conf_file = os.path.join(args.src_dir, "dxasset.json")
196	
197	        dxpy.api.system_whoami()
198	        dest_project_name, dest_folder_name, dest_asset_name = parse_destination(args.destination)
199	        if dest_project_name is None:
200	            raise AssetBuilderException("Can't build an asset without specifying a destination project; \
201	            please use the -d/--destination flag to explicitly specify a project")
202	        if dest_asset_name is None:
203	            dest_asset_name = asset_conf['name']
204	
205	        # If dx build_asset is launched form a job, set json flag to True to avoid watching the job log
206	        if dxpy.JOB_ID:
207	            args.json = True
208	
209	        if not args.json:
210	            print("Uploading input files for the AssetBuilder", file=sys.stderr)
211	
212	        conf_file = dx_upload(asset_conf_file, dest_project_name, dest_folder_name, args.json)
213	        make_file = get_asset_make(args.src_dir, dest_project_name, dest_folder_name, args.json)
214	        asset_file = get_asset_tarball(asset_conf['name'], args.src_dir, dest_project_name,
215	                                       dest_folder_name, args.json)
216	
217	        input_hash = {"conf_json": dxpy.dxlink(conf_file)}
218	        if asset_file:
219	            input_hash["custom_asset"] = dxpy.dxlink(asset_file)
220	        if make_file:
221	            input_hash["asset_makefile"] = dxpy.dxlink(make_file)
222	
223	        builder_run_options = {
224	            "name": dest_asset_name,
225	            "input": input_hash
226	            }
227	
228	        if args.priority is not None:
229	            builder_run_options["priority"] = args.priority
230	
231	        # Add the default destination project to app run options, if it is not run from a job
232	        if not dxpy.JOB_ID:
233	            builder_run_options["project"] = dest_project_name
234	        if 'instanceType' in asset_conf:
235	            builder_run_options["systemRequirements"] = {"*": {"instanceType": asset_conf["instanceType"]}}
236	        if dest_folder_name:
237	            builder_run_options["folder"] = dest_folder_name
238	
239	        release = asset_conf['release']
240	        if asset_conf['runSpecVersion'] == '1':
241	            release += '_v1'
242	        app_run_result = dxpy.api.app_run(ASSET_BUILDERS[release], input_params=builder_run_options)
243	
244	        job_id = app_run_result["id"]
245	
246	        if not args.json:
247	            print("\nStarted job '" + str(job_id) + "' to build the asset bundle.\n", file=sys.stderr)
248	            if args.watch:
249	                try:
250	                    subprocess.check_call(["dx", "watch", job_id])
251	                except subprocess.CalledProcessError as e:
252	                    if e.returncode == 3:
253	                        # Some kind of failure to build the asset. The reason
254	                        # for the failure is probably self-evident from the
255	                        # job log (and if it's not, the CalledProcessError
256	                        # is not informative anyway), so just propagate the
257	                        # return code without additional remarks.
258	                        sys.exit(3)
259	                    else:
260	                        raise e
261	
262	        dxpy.DXJob(job_id).wait_on_done(interval=1)
263	        asset_id, _ = dxpy.get_dxlink_ids(dxpy.api.job_describe(job_id)['output']['asset_bundle'])
264	
265	        if args.json:
266	            print(json.dumps({"id": asset_id}))
267	        else:
268	            print("\nAsset bundle '" + asset_id +
269	                  "' is built and can now be used in your app/applet's dxapp.json\n", file=sys.stderr)
270	    except Exception as de:
271	        print(de.__class__.__name__ + ": " + str(de), file=sys.stderr)
272	        sys.exit(1)
273	    finally:
274	        if conf_file:
275	            try:
276	                conf_file.remove()
277	            except:
278	                pass
279	        if make_file:
280	            try:
281	                make_file.remove()
282	            except:
283	                pass
284	        if asset_file:
285	            try:
286	                asset_file.remove()
287	            except:
288	                pass

2	from collections import defaultdict
3	import copy
4	
5	from .utils import merge
6	from .exceptions import (err_exit, DXError, DXCLIError)
7	from .compat import basestring
8	
9	'''
10	System Requirements
11	+++++++++++++++++++
12	
13	A module containing utility methods useful for packing and unpacking
14	system requirements.
15	'''
16	
17	class SystemRequirementsDict(object):
18	    """
19	    A class representing system requirements that can be passed as
20	    "systemRequirements" or an entry of the "systemRequirementsByExecutable"
21	    to the class-xxxx/run or job/new API call (after converting
22	    it to a dictionary with as_dict()).
23	    """
24	
25	    def __init__(self, entrypoints):
26	        """
27	        Example of the entrypoints input:
28	        {"main":
29	            {"instanceType": "mem2_hdd2_x2"},
30	         "other_function":
31	            {"instanceType": "mem2_hdd2_x1",
32	             "clusterSpec": {"type": "spark",
33	                             "version": "2.4.0",
34	                             "initialInstanceCount": 2}}}
35	        """
36	        if entrypoints is not None and not isinstance(entrypoints, dict):
37	            raise DXError("Expected entrypoints to be a dict or None")
38	        self.entrypoints = copy.deepcopy(entrypoints)
39	
40	    @classmethod
41	    def from_instance_count(cls, instance_count_arg, entrypoint="*"):
42	        """
43	        Returns a SystemRequirementsDict that can be passed as a
44	        "systemRequirements" input or an entry of the "systemRequirementsByExecutable" mapping
45	        to job/new or run/ API calls.
46	        The instance_count_arg should be either a:
47	        * string or int eg. "6" or 8
48	        * dictionary, eg. {"main": 4, "other_function": 2}
49	        """
50	        try:
51	            if instance_count_arg is None:
52	                return cls(None)
53	            if isinstance(instance_count_arg, basestring) or isinstance(instance_count_arg, int):
54	                return cls({entrypoint: {"clusterSpec": {"initialInstanceCount": int(instance_count_arg)}}})
55	            if isinstance(instance_count_arg, dict):
56	                return cls({k: {"clusterSpec": {"initialInstanceCount": int(v)}} for k, v in instance_count_arg.items()})
57	            raise ValueError
58	        except ValueError:
59	            DXError('Expected instance_count field to be either an int, string or a dict')
60	
61	    @classmethod
62	    def from_instance_type(cls, instance_type_arg, entrypoint="*"):
63	        """
64	        Returns SystemRequirementsDict that can be passed as a
65	        "systemRequirements" input or an entry of the "systemRequirementsByExecutable" mapping
66	        to job/new or run/ API calls.
67	        The instance_type_arg should be either a:
68	        * string, eg. mem1_ssd1_x2
69	        * dictionary, eg. {"main": "mem2_hdd2_x2", "other_function": "mem2_hdd2_x1"}
70	        """
71	        if instance_type_arg is None:
72	            return cls(None)
73	        if isinstance(instance_type_arg, basestring):
74	            # By default, all entry points ("*") should use this instance type
75	            return cls({entrypoint: {"instanceType": instance_type_arg}})
76	        if isinstance(instance_type_arg, dict):
77	            # instance_type is a map of entry point to instance type
78	            return cls({fn: {"instanceType": fn_inst} for fn, fn_inst in instance_type_arg.items()})
79	        raise DXError('Expected instance_type field to be either a string or a dict')
80	
81	    @classmethod
82	    def from_sys_requirements(cls, system_requirements, _type='all'):
83	        """
84	        Returns SystemRequirementsDict encapsulating system requirements.
85	        It can extract only entrypoints with specific fields ('clusterSpec',
86	        'instanceType', 'instanceTypeSelector', etc), depending on the value of _type.
87	        """
88	        allowed_types = ['all', 'clusterSpec', 'instanceType', 'instanceTypeSelector', 'fpgaDriver', 'nvidiaDriver']
89	        if _type not in (allowed_types):
90	            raise DXError("Expected '_type' to be one of the following: {}".format(allowed_types))
91	
92	        if _type == 'all':
93	            return cls(system_requirements)
94	
95	        extracted = defaultdict(dict)
96	        for entrypoint, req in system_requirements.items():
97	            if _type in req:
98	                extracted[entrypoint][_type] = req[_type]
99	        return cls(dict(extracted))
100	
101	    def override_cluster_spec(self, srd):
102	        """
103	        Returns SystemRequirementsDict can be passed in a "systemRequirements"
104	        input or as an entry of the "systemRequirementsByExecutable" mapping
105	        to app-xxx/run, e.g. {'fn': {'clusterSpec': {initialInstanceCount: 3, version: "2.4.0", ..}}}
106	        Since full clusterSpec must be passed to the API server, we need to retrieve the cluster
107	        spec defined in app doc's systemRequirements and overwrite the field initialInstanceCount
108	        with the value the user passed to dx run for each entrypoint.
109	        initialInstanceCount is currently the only clusterSpec's field the user is allowed to change
110	        at runtime.
111	        A few scenarios when requesting instance count for different entrypoints with dx run 
112	        and the resulting merged systemRequirements (merged_cluster_spec). The bootstapScript
113	        field here is only one of many (version, ports, etc) that should be copied from app
114	        spec to merged_cluster_spec:
115	
116	        Requested: {"*": 5}
117	        App doc: {"main": "clusterSpec": {"initialInstanceCount": 7, bootstrapScript: "x.sh"},
118	                "other": "clusterSpec": {"initialInstanceCount": 9, bootstrapScript: "y.sh"}}
119	        Merged: {"main": "clusterSpec": {"initialInstanceCount": 5, bootstrapScript: "x.sh"},
120	                "other": "clusterSpec": {"initialInstanceCount": 5, bootstrapScript: "y.sh"}}
121	        
122	        Requested: {"*": 15}
123	        App doc: {"main": "clusterSpec": {"initialInstanceCount": 7, bootstrapScript: "x.sh"},
124	                  "other": "clusterSpec": {"initialInstanceCount": 9, bootstrapScript: "y.sh"},
125	                  "*": "clusterSpec": {"initialInstanceCount": 11, bootstrapScript: "y.sh"}}
126	        Merged: {"main": "clusterSpec": {"initialInstanceCount": 15, bootstrapScript: "x.sh"},
127	                 "other": "clusterSpec": {"initialInstanceCount": 15, bootstrapScript: "y.sh"},
128	                 "*": "clusterSpec": {"initialInstanceCount": 15, bootstrapScript: "y.sh"}}
129	
130	        Requested: {"main": 12}
131	        App doc: {"main": "clusterSpec": {"initialInstanceCount": 7, bootstrapScript: "x.sh"},
132	                  "other": "clusterSpec": {"initialInstanceCount": 9, bootstrapScript: "y.sh"}}
133	        Merged: {"main": "clusterSpec": {"initialInstanceCount": 12, bootstrapScript: "x.sh"}}
134	
135	        Requested: {"main": 33}
136	        App doc: {"*": "clusterSpec": {"initialInstanceCount": 2, bootstrapScript: "z.sh"}}
137	        Merged: {"main": "clusterSpec": {"initialInstanceCount": 33, bootstrapScript: "z.sh"}}
138	
139	        Requested: {"main": 22, "*": 11}
140	        App doc: {"*": "clusterSpec": {"initialInstanceCount": 2, bootstrapScript: "t.sh"}}
141	        Merged: {"main": "clusterSpec": {"initialInstanceCount": 22, bootstrapScript: "t.sh"},
142	                 "*": "clusterSpec": {"initialInstanceCount": 11, bootstrapScript: "t.sh"}}
143	        """
144	
145	        merged_cluster_spec = copy.deepcopy(self.entrypoints)
146	
147	        # Remove entrypoints without "clusterSpec"
148	        merged_cluster_spec = dict([(k, v) for k, v in merged_cluster_spec.items() if v.get("clusterSpec") is not None])
149	
150	        # Remove entrypoints not provided in requested instance counts
151	        merged_cluster_spec = dict([(k, v) for k, v in merged_cluster_spec.items() if \
152	            k in srd.entrypoints or "*" in srd.entrypoints])
153	
154	        # Overwrite values of self.entrypoints.clusterSpec with the ones from srd
155	        # Named entrypoint takes precedence over the wildcard
156	        for entry_pt, req in merged_cluster_spec.items():
157	            merged_cluster_spec[entry_pt]["clusterSpec"].update(
158	                srd.entrypoints.get(entry_pt, srd.entrypoints.get("*"))["clusterSpec"])
159	
160	        # Check if all entrypoints in srd are included in merged_cluster_spec
161	        # (if a named entrypoint was used in srd and such an entrypoint doesn't exist
162	        #  in app sys req, we need to take the cluster spec from the app's "*", if it exists)
163	        for entry_pt, req in srd.entrypoints.items():
164	            if entry_pt not in merged_cluster_spec and "*" in self.entrypoints and "clusterSpec" in self.entrypoints["*"]:
165	                merged_cluster_spec[entry_pt] = {"clusterSpec": copy.deepcopy(self.entrypoints["*"]["clusterSpec"])}
166	                merged_cluster_spec[entry_pt]["clusterSpec"].update(req["clusterSpec"])
167	
168	        return SystemRequirementsDict(merged_cluster_spec)
169	
170	    def override_spec(self, requested_spec):
171	        if "*" in requested_spec.as_dict():
172	            return requested_spec
173	        
174	        entrypoints = self.entrypoints.keys() | requested_spec.entrypoints.keys()
175	        merged_spec = dict.fromkeys(entrypoints)
176	        for e in entrypoints:
177	            merged_spec[e] = requested_spec.entrypoints.get(e) or requested_spec.entrypoints.get("*") or self.entrypoints.get(e) or self.entrypoints.get("*")
178	        return SystemRequirementsDict(merged_spec)
179	
180	    def _add_dict_values(self, d1, d2):
181	        """
182	        Merges the values of two dictionaries, which are expected to be dictionaries, e.g
183	        d1 = {'a': {'x': pqr}}
184	        d2 = {'a': {'y': lmn}, 'b': {'y': rst}}
185	        will return: {'a': {'x': pqr, 'y': lmn}, 'b': {'y': rst}}.
186	        Collisions of the keys of the sub-dictionaries are not checked.
187	        """
188	
189	        if d1 is None and d2 is None:
190	            return None
191	
192	        d1 = d1 or {}
193	        d2 = d2 or {}
194	
195	        added = {}
196	        for key in set(list(d1.keys()) + list(d2.keys())):
197	            added[key] = dict(d1.get(key, {}), **(d2.get(key, {})))
198	        return added
199	
200	    def __add__(self, other):
201	        if not isinstance(other, SystemRequirementsDict):
202	            raise DXError("Developer error: SystemRequirementsDict expected")
203	        added_entrypoints = self._add_dict_values(self.entrypoints, other.entrypoints)
204	        return SystemRequirementsDict(added_entrypoints)
205	
206	    def as_dict(self):
207	        return self.entrypoints

21	from .utils.printing import (RED, BOLD)
22	from .exceptions import err_exit
23	from .utils.resolver import get_app_from_path
24	
25	from sys import platform
26	NOTEBOOK_APP = '_notebook_server'
27	LOUPE_APP = '_10x_loupe_server'
28	SERVER_READY_TAG = 'server_running'
29	SLEEP_PERIOD = 5
30	
31	def setup_ssh_tunnel(job_id, local_port, remote_port):
32	    """
33	    Setup an ssh tunnel to the given job-id.  This will establish
34	    the port over the given local_port to the given remote_port
35	    and then exit, keeping the tunnel in place until the job is
36	    terminated.
37	    """
38	    cmd = ['dx', 'ssh', '--suppress-running-check', job_id, '-o', 'StrictHostKeyChecking no']
39	    cmd += ['-f', '-L', '{0}:localhost:{1}'.format(local_port, remote_port), '-N']
40	    subprocess.check_call(cmd)
41	
42	
43	def poll_for_server_running(job_id):
44	    """
45	    Poll for the job to start running and post the SERVER_READY_TAG.
46	    """
47	    sys.stdout.write('Waiting for server in {0} to initialize ...'.format(job_id))
48	    sys.stdout.flush()
49	    desc = dxpy.describe(job_id)
50	    # Keep checking until the server has begun or it has failed.
51	    while(SERVER_READY_TAG not in desc['tags'] and desc['state'] != 'failed'):
52	        time.sleep(SLEEP_PERIOD)
53	        sys.stdout.write('.')
54	        sys.stdout.flush()
55	        desc = dxpy.describe(job_id)
56	
57	    # If the server job failed, provide friendly advice.
58	    if desc['state'] == 'failed':
59	        msg = RED('Error:') + ' Server failed to run.\n'
60	        msg += 'You may want to check the job logs by running:'
61	        msg += BOLD('dx watch {0}'.format(job_id))
62	        err_exit(msg)
63	
64	
65	def multi_platform_open(cmd):
66	    """
67	    Take the given command and use the OS to automatically open the appropriate
68	    resource.  For instance, if a URL is provided, this will have the OS automatically
69	    open the URL in the default web browser.
70	    """
71	    if platform == "linux" or platform == "linux2":
72	        cmd = ['xdg-open', cmd]
73	    elif platform == "darwin":
74	        cmd = ['open', cmd]
75	    elif platform == "win32":
76	        cmd = ['start', cmd]
77	    subprocess.check_call(cmd)
78	
79	
80	def get_notebook_app_versions():
81	    """
82	    Get the valid version numbers of the notebook app.
83	    """
84	    notebook_apps = dxpy.find_apps(name=NOTEBOOK_APP, all_versions=True)
85	    versions = [str(dxpy.describe(app['id'])['version']) for app in notebook_apps]
86	    return versions
87	
88	
89	def run_notebook(args, ssh_config_check):
90	    """
91	    Launch the notebook server.
92	    """
93	    # Check that ssh is setup.  Currently notebooks require ssh for tunelling.
94	    ssh_config_check()
95	    if args.only_check_config:
96	        return
97	
98	    # If the user requested a specific version of the notebook server,
99	    # get the executable id.
100	    if args.version is not None:
101	        executable = get_app_from_path('app-{0}/{1}'.format(NOTEBOOK_APP, args.version))
102	        if executable is not None and 'id' in executable:
103	            executable = executable['id']
104	        else:
105	            msg = RED('Warning:') + ' Invalid notebook version: {0}\nValid versions are: '.format(args.version)
106	            msg += BOLD('{0}'.format(str(get_notebook_app_versions())))
107	            err_exit(msg)
108	    else:
109	        executable = 'app-{0}'.format(NOTEBOOK_APP)
110	
111	    # Compose the command to launch the notebook
112	    cmd = ['dx', 'run', executable, '-inotebook_type={0}'.format(args.notebook_type)]
113	    cmd += ['-iinput_files={0}'.format(f) for f in args.notebook_files]
114	    cmd += ['-itimeout={0}'.format(args.timeout), '-y', '--brief', '--allow-ssh', '--instance-type', args.instance_type]
115	    if args.spark:
116	        cmd += ['-iinstall_spark=true']
117	    if args.snapshot:
118	        cmd += ['-isnapshot={0}'.format(args.snapshot)]
119	    job_id = subprocess.check_output(cmd).strip()
120	
121	    poll_for_server_running(job_id)
122	
123	    if args.notebook_type in {'jupyter', 'jupyter_lab', 'jupyter_notebook'}:
124	        remote_port = 8888
125	
126	    setup_ssh_tunnel(job_id, args.port, remote_port)
127	
128	    if args.open_server:

292	    :param arg_parser: argparse.ArgumentParser object used in the program (optional)

295	    :param exception: an exception to use in place of the last exception raised
296	    '''

301	    if isinstance(exc, SystemExit):

303	    elif isinstance(exc, expected_exceptions):
304	        exit_with_exc_info(EXPECTED_ERR_EXIT_STATUS, message, print_tb=dxpy._DEBUG > 0, exception=exception)
305	    elif ignore_sigpipe and isinstance(exc, IOError) and getattr(exc, 'errno', None) == errno.EPIPE:
306	        if dxpy._DEBUG > 0:
307	            print("Broken pipe", file=sys.stderr)
308	        sys.exit(3)
309	    else:
310	        if code is None:
311	            code = 1

46	def which(program):
47	    def is_exe(fpath):
48	        return os.path.isfile(fpath) and os.access(fpath, os.X_OK)
49

70	class DXPYTestsRunner:
71	    dx_toolkit: Path
72	    token: str
73	    env: str = "stg"
74	    pyenv_filters_inclusive: Optional[List[Matcher]] = None
75	    pyenv_filters_exclusive: Optional[List[Matcher]] = None
76	    extra_requirements: Optional[List[str]] = None
77	    pytest_args: Optional[str] = None
78	    report: Optional[str] = None
79	    logs_dir: str = Path("logs")
80	    workers: int = 1
81	    retries: int = 1
82	    print_logs: bool = False
83	    print_failed_logs: bool = False
84	    _macos_version: float = float('.'.join(platform.mac_ver()[0].split('.')[:2]))
85	    _brew_in_opt: bool = Path("/opt/homebrew").is_dir()
86	    _test_results: Dict[str, Dict] = field(default_factory=dict, init=False)
87	
88	    def __post_init__(self):
89	        self.dx_toolkit = self.dx_toolkit.absolute()
90	        self.logs_dir = self.logs_dir.absolute()
91	        logging.debug(f"Detected MacOS version {self._macos_version}")
92	
93	    def run(self):
94	        pyenvs = filter_pyenvs(PYENVS, self.pyenv_filters_inclusive, self.pyenv_filters_exclusive)
95	
96	        logging.info("Python environments: " + ", ".join(pyenvs))
97	
98	        for pyenv in pyenvs:
99	            p = PyEnv(pyenv)
100	            if p.is_pyenv:
101	                logging.info(f"[{pyenv}] Installing Python {p.python_version} using pyenv")
102	                with open(self.logs_dir / f"{pyenv}_install.log", 'w') as fh:
103	                    subprocess.run(["pyenv", "install", "--skip-existing", p.python_version], check=True, stdout=fh, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT, text=True)
104	            elif p.is_brew:
105	                logging.info(f"[{pyenv}] Installing Python {p.python_version} using brew")
106	                with open(self.logs_dir / f"{pyenv}_install.log", 'w') as fh:
107	                    subprocess.run(["brew", "install", "--overwrite", "--force", f"python@{p.python_version}"], check=True, stdout=fh, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT, text=True)
108	
109	        with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=self.workers) as executor:
110	            for pyenv in pyenvs:
111	                executor.submit(self._run_pyenv, pyenv)
112	            executor.shutdown(wait=True)
113	
114	        exit_code = make_execution_summary(self._test_results, self.report)
115	        return exit_code
116	
117	    def _store_test_results(self, pyenv, code, failed_tests=None):
118	        self._test_results[pyenv] = {
119	            "code": code,
120	            "failed_tests": failed_tests
121	        }
122	        with open(self.logs_dir / f"{pyenv}.status", 'w') as fh:
123	            fh.write(f"{code}\n")
124	
125	    def _run_pyenv(self, pyenv: str):
126	        try:
127	            for i in range(1, self.retries + 1):
128	                try:
129	                    self._do_run_pyenv(pyenv)
130	                    break
131	                except:
132	                    if i == self.retries:
133	                        raise
134	                    logging.exception(f"[{pyenv}] Tests execution failed (try {i})")
135	                    time.sleep(random.randrange(70, 90))
136	        except:
137	            logging.exception(f"[{pyenv} Failed running tests")
138	            self._store_test_results(pyenv, EXIT_TEST_EXECUTION_FAILED)
139	
140	    def _do_run_pyenv(self, pyenv: str):
141	        p = PyEnv(pyenv)
142	        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as wd:
143	            logging.info(f"[{pyenv}] Preparing for test execution (temporary dir: '{wd}')")
144	            wd = Path(wd)
145	
146	            dx_python_root = wd / "python"
147	            shutil.copytree(self.dx_toolkit / "src" / "python", dx_python_root)
148	
149	            env = os.environ.copy()
150	
151	            if p.is_system:
152	                env["DXPY_TEST_BASE_PYTHON_BIN"] = f"/usr/bin/python3"
153	            elif p.is_official:
154	                env["DXPY_TEST_BASE_PYTHON_BIN"] = str(Path("/Library") / "Frameworks" / "Python.framework" / "Versions" / p.python_version / "bin" / f"python{p.python_version}")
155	            elif p.is_pyenv:
156	                subprocess.run(f"pyenv local {p.python_version}", cwd=wd, check=True, shell=True, stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT)
157	                env["DXPY_TEST_USING_PYENV"] = "true"
158	            elif p.is_brew:
159	                if self._brew_in_opt:
160	                    env["DXPY_TEST_BASE_PYTHON_BIN"] = str(Path("/opt") / "homebrew" / "bin" / f"python{p.python_version}")
161	                else:
162	                    env["DXPY_TEST_BASE_PYTHON_BIN"] = str(Path("/usr") / "local" / "opt" / f"python@{p.python_version}" / "bin" / f"python{p.python_version}")
163	
164	            if self.extra_requirements and len(self.extra_requirements) > 0:
165	                extra_requirements_file = wd / "extra_requirements.txt"
166	                with open(extra_requirements_file, 'w') as fh:
167	                    fh.writelines(self.extra_requirements)
168	                env["DXPY_TEST_EXTRA_REQUIREMENTS"] = str(extra_requirements_file)
169	
170	            env_dir = wd / "testenv"
171	
172	            logging.info(f"[{pyenv}] Running tests")
173	            env["DXPY_TEST_TOKEN"] = self.token
174	            env["DXPY_TEST_PYTHON_VERSION"] = p.python_version[0]
175	            env["DX_USER_CONF_DIR"] = str((wd / ".dnanexus_config").absolute())
176	            tests_log: Path = self.logs_dir / f"{pyenv}_test.log"
177	            with open(tests_log, 'w') as fh:
178	                res = subprocess.run([ROOT_DIR / "macos" / "run_tests.sh", dx_python_root, env_dir] + (self.pytest_args or []), env=env, cwd=wd, stdout=fh, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT, stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL)
179	            if res.returncode != 0:
180	                logging.error(f"[{pyenv}] Tests exited with non-zero code. See log for console output: {tests_log.absolute()}")
181	                if self.print_logs or self.print_failed_logs:
182	                    self._print_log(pyenv, tests_log)

1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	
3	'''
4	Runs Python integration tests
5	
6	Assumes  `make python src_libs && source build/py_env/bin/activate`
7	
8	If no arguments are given, all tests in src/python/test/ are run.
9	
10	To run a single test method, e.g. test_basic in class TestDXBashHelpers,
11	in file src/python/test/test_dx_bash_helpers.py:
12	
13	    $ build/run_python_integration_tests.py --tests test_dx_bash_helpers.TestDXBashHelpers.test_basic
14	
15	To run an entire test class:
16	
17	    $ build/run_python_integration_tests.py --tests test_dx_bash_helpers.TestDXBashHelpers
18	
19	To run all tests in a file:
20	
21	    $ build/run_python_integration_tests.py --tests test_dx_bash_helpers
22	'''
23	
24	from __future__ import print_function, unicode_literals
25	
26	import argparse
27	import os
28	import platform
29	import subprocess
30	import sys
31	
32	parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(usage=__doc__)
33	parser.add_argument(
34	    '--tests',
35	    help='Specify a specific test to run.',
36	    metavar='test_module.TestCase.test_method',
37	    nargs='*'
38	)
39	
40	TOOLKIT_ROOT_DIR = os.path.abspath(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.realpath(__file__)), '..'))
41	PYTHON_DIR = os.path.join(TOOLKIT_ROOT_DIR, 'src', 'python')
42	PYTHON_TEST_DIR = os.path.join(PYTHON_DIR, 'test')
43	os.environ['DNANEXUS_INSTALL_PYTHON_TEST_DEPS'] = 'yes'
44	
45	def run():
46	    # Assumes `make python src_libs` has been run
47	
48	    cmd = ['python3', '-m', 'unittest']
49	    if args.tests:
50	        cmd += ['-v'] + args.tests
51	    else:
52	        cmd += ['discover', '--start-directory', '.', '--verbose']
53	
54	    if platform.system() == 'Windows':
55	        # Grab existing env vars with nt.environ, so that the SystemRoot var
56	        # isn't uppercased - because that can cause _urandom() errors. See:
57	        #   http://bugs.python.org/issue1384175#msg248951
58	        import nt
59	        subproc_env = dict(nt.environ)
60	    else:
61	        subproc_env = dict(os.environ)
62	
63	    try:
64	        subprocess.check_call(cmd, cwd=PYTHON_TEST_DIR, env=subproc_env)
65	    except subprocess.CalledProcessError as e:
66	        print('*** unittest invocation failed with code %d' % (e.returncode,), file=sys.stderr)
67	        sys.exit(1)
68	
69	if __name__ == '__main__':
70	    args = parser.parse_args()
71	    run()
72

110	        the time -- hence the deepcopy here instead of inspecting the mock afterward.

9483	            - returns the ID of the resource bundle (when extract_resources is False)

9490

9493	
9494	        # download resources tar and extract it to a temp. directory.
9495	        # note that if the resource directory also contains a file of the name
9496	        # './res.tar.gz', things could get ugly, but this is just a helper for

95	def _dump_app_or_applet(executable, omit_resources=False, describe_output={}):
96	    info = executable.get()
97	
98	    if info["runSpec"]["interpreter"] == "bash":
99	        suffix = "sh"
100	    elif info["runSpec"]["interpreter"].startswith("python"):
101	        suffix = "py"
102	    else:
103	        print("Sorry, I don\'t know how to get executables with interpreter {}.\n".format(
104	            info["runSpec"]["interpreter"]), file=sys.stderr)
105	        sys.exit(1)
106	
107	    # Entry point script
108	    script = "src/code.{}".format(suffix)
109	    os.mkdir("src")
110	    with open(script, "w") as f:
111	        f.write(info["runSpec"]["code"])

113	    def make_cluster_bootstrap_script_file(region, entry_point, code, suffix):
114	        """
115	        Writes the string `code` into a file at the relative path
116	        "src/<region>_<entry_point>_clusterBootstrap.<suffix>"
117	        """
118	        script_name = "src/{}_{}_clusterBootstrap.{}".format(region, entry_point, suffix)
119	        with open(script_name, "w") as f:
120	            f.write(code)
121	        return script_name
122	    
123	    # Get regions where the user's billTo are permitted
124	    try:
125	        bill_to = dxpy.api.user_describe(dxpy.whoami())['billTo']
126	        permitted_regions = set(dxpy.DXHTTPRequest('/' + bill_to + '/describe', {}).get("permittedRegions"))
127	    except DXError:
128	        print("Failed to get permitted regions where {} can perform billable activities.\n".format(bill_to), file=sys.stderr)
129	        sys.exit(1)    
130	    
131	    # when applet/app is built, the runSpec is initialized with fields "interpreter" and "bundledDependsByRegion"
132	    # even when we don't have any bundledDepends in dxapp.json
